result.summary:
I read all of configuration.md: the intake sections closely, and the provider, reranker, auth and storage blocks by keyword search. I checked it against the feature matrix, the recorded resolved bank config and Atlas's retain code. Atlas's bank runs Hindsight's intake defaults: concise extraction, 3,000-character chunks, free-form fuzzy entity resolution, no strategies, no labels and no item entities. Atlas overrides only the missions and dispositions.

The levers that matter most:
1. Atlas embeds with qwen3-embedding-0.6b through the `openai` provider. That provider never adds the search instruction Qwen3 needs, and Atlas sets no `EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_PREFIX`.
2. Atlas's `observations_mission` replaces the built-in consolidation rules entirely.
3. Entity resolution is fuzzy. Its 7-day temporal signal is useless for filings months apart, while Atlas already holds canonical company identities it could pass in as entities or labels.
4. Retain strategies give per-call extraction profiles (mode, mission, chunk size, labels), which fit per-document-type batches. The dry-run extract endpoint makes them cheap to test.
5. `FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS` is off, so facts can be dropped silently.
6. The five similarity gates were calibrated for a different embedding model.
7. Consolidation can get its own per-operation LLM chain.

Entity-label format, `observation_scopes` values and how chunks are split live in retain.md and api/*, which I did not read.

findings.statement: Qwen3-Embedding models expect an instruction in front of each search query. Hindsight adds it automatically only with the `local` provider. For plain-text providers (openai, tei, litellm) the operator must set HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_PREFIX (and PASSAGE_PREFIX if needed). This is a static server setting. An instruction on the search side only needs no re-indexing.
findings.quote: The default `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` ships none, so nothing changes for existing deployments; `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-*` ships one for searches only, which is what makes those models retrieve accurately.
findings.atlas_today: compose.yaml (which states it mirrors the cluster) runs qwen3-embedding-0.6b through HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=openai via LiteLLM and sets no QUERY_PREFIX, so recall queries and Scout pointer queries are embedded without the instruction. I did not verify the cluster env in home-ops.
findings.opportunity: Set HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_PREFIX to Qwen3's query instruction on the server, with no re-index. Then compare recall and pointer quality before and after on the pilot question set.

findings.topic: Embeddings: similarity gates calibrated for another model
findings.statement: Five cosine gates were calibrated for bge-small-en-v1.5 and the docs say to recalibrate all of them after a model change: semantic retrieval 0.3, graph seed 0.3, temporal 0.1, semantic links at retain 0.7, observation dedup 0.97. All are server env. The semantic-link threshold acts at retain time and is not applied retroactively.
findings.quote: configured independently. Their defaults preserve the behavior calibrated for `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`.
findings.atlas_today: Atlas uses qwen3-embedding-0.6b at 1024 dims with every gate at its default (none set in compose.yaml).
findings.opportunity: Measure the cosine distributions of qwen3 on Atlas's facts and recalibrate the gates, above all SEMANTIC_LINK_MIN_SIMILARITY, which sets graph density for every future retain. Do it before the bulk universe backfill, because it is not retroactive.

findings.topic: Consolidation: observations_mission replaces the built-in rules
findings.statement: Setting observations_mission (per bank or server) replaces Hindsight's default definition of an observation entirely. The default definition is durable, specific beliefs grounded in source memories, ephemeral state filtered out, and contradictions tracked with temporal markers rather than overwritten. Only the bank's mission text then guides what consolidation creates or updates.
findings.quote: Set `HINDSIGHT_API_OBSERVATIONS_MISSION` to replace this definition entirely.
findings.atlas_today: configs/hindsight/bank-template.json sets a one-sentence observations_mission ("Consolidate independently grounded industry developments while recording contradictions, conditionality and changed circumstances..."), so the default rules are gone.
findings.opportunity: Rewrite the mission so it carries what Atlas needs from the defaults: per-company specificity, temporal markers on changed facts (as of which filing or period), keeping figures with unit and period, and supplier/customer relationships. Observations are what reflect cites and what Atlas resolves through source_memory_ids.

findings.topic: Entity resolution: fuzzy matching, 7-day temporal signal
findings.statement: An extracted name is matched against existing entities in two stages. Stage 1: trigram ≥ 0.15, at most 200 candidates. Stage 2: a candidate is reused if its score clears 0.6, from name similarity (up to 0.5), co-occurring entities (up to 0.3) and temporal proximity (up to 0.2, decaying to zero at 7 days from the candidate's last_seen). It must also reach a trigram floor of 0.3 and agree word by word. Label entities resolve by exact match only. All thresholds are server env.
findings.quote: How close the fact's date is to the candidate's `last_seen`, decaying linearly to zero at 7 days
findings.atlas_today: Atlas relies on free-form fuzzy resolution. Its filings are dated by available_at, months apart, so the temporal signal contributes nothing. Name variants such as 'Coherent Corp.', 'Coherent' and 'II-VI' must merge on name and co-occurrence alone, or stay separate entities.
findings.opportunity: Give Hindsight Atlas's resolved identities so graph expansion (entity co-occurrence) follows real companies across filings: user-provided item entities with resolve_entities false, or per-bank entity_labels. See the next finding.

findings.statement: entity_labels (a controlled vocabulary) and entities_allow_free_form (default true) are set per bank, not by env, and can also be overridden per retain strategy. Both appear in the bank-template schema. Items can carry their own entities (RetainContent.entities). In chunks mode these are the only entity data.
findings.quote: are configured per bank via the [bank config API](api/memory-banks.md#retain-configuration), not as global environment variables
findings.atlas_today: Resolved config shows entity_labels null and entities_allow_free_form true. RetainItem in backend/atlas/hindsight/models.py has no entities field.
findings.opportunity: Add the universe and counterparty companies (canonical names) to each section's retain item as entities, or as a label vocabulary in the template. Then entity links in the graph and co-occurrence match Atlas's identity layer, which multi-hop supply-chain recall depends on. Check the field format in api/retain.md first.

findings.statement: A bank can define named retain_strategies, each a set of hierarchical overrides (extraction mode, chunk size, structured chunk size, entity_labels, free-form, retain_mission, ...). A retain call picks one with `strategy`; otherwise retain_default_strategy applies. The docs show the strategy chosen per call, not per item.
findings.quote: Named strategies let you ingest different content types into the same bank using different extraction settings. A strategy is a set of hierarchical field overrides applied on top of the resolved bank config.
findings.atlas_today: No strategies are defined. The gateway posts {items, async: true} with no strategy, so 10-K Items, 8-K exhibits and TradingView transcripts all get one mission and the concise mode.
findings.opportunity: Define strategies per document type in the bank template. For example, a transcript mission for management statements on capacity, customers and lead times, verbose mode for exhibits and press releases, and the filings mission for 10-K/10-Q Items. Pass `strategy` per batch (Atlas batches per Source Version already). Compare strategies first with the dry-run extract endpoint.

findings.statement: retain_extraction_mode is one of concise (the default), verbose, verbatim, chunks or custom. It can be set on the server, per bank or per strategy. Verbose gives richer facts that keep context and relationships, at more tokens. Verbatim stores each chunk exactly as one memory and still runs the LLM for entities, time and place. Chunks makes no LLM call. Custom replaces the selectivity rules but keeps output format, temporal handling and coreference.
findings.quote: Each chunk is stored as a single memory unit with its original text preserved exactly — no summarization or rewriting.
findings.atlas_today: concise (resolved config recording). Atlas never quotes memory text: the memories only choose sections.
findings.opportunity: Atlas uses memories only as pointers to sections, so verbose (relationship qualifiers kept) or verbatim (the chunk text itself indexed, entities still extracted) could make better pointers. Try them per strategy on recorded filings with dry-run extract before changing the bank.

findings.statement: By default a retain whose fact extraction hit errors is still marked completed, and the facts it lost are dropped silently. With HINDSIGHT_API_FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS=true such a retain is marked failed, with the error count. It is a static server setting.
findings.quote: When `true`, a retain operation that accumulated any fact-extraction errors is marked `failed` (with an error message including the count) instead of `completed`, so silently-dropped facts surface as a hard failure.
findings.atlas_today: Not set (default false). Atlas's poll_operation treats completed as retained, so a long Item with a failed chunk would look fully retained.
findings.opportunity: Set it to true on the server. Atlas's retain/poll path already retries failed operations, so lost chunks become retries instead of gaps in the index.

findings.statement: Extraction runs one LLM call per chunk of at most retain_chunk_size characters (default 3000; server, bank or strategy). Each chunk yields roughly 17 facts. Chunk boundaries and token counts use HINDSIGHT_API_TOKENIZER_ENCODING (o200k_base). This page documents no overlap setting and no boundary rule.
findings.quote: Max characters per chunk for fact extraction. Larger chunks extract fewer LLM calls but may lose context.
findings.atlas_today: Default 3000. Atlas sections are whole SEC Items (often tens of thousands of characters) or chunks of up to MAX_CHUNK_CHARS = 12_000, so Hindsight re-splits each one. Each 3000-character piece is extracted with only the item's `context` ('title: heading') as document-level framing.
findings.opportunity: Tune retain_chunk_size per strategy (e.g. larger for transcripts, so a Q&A answer stays with its question). Check in retain.md whether `context` reaches every chunk's prompt. Atlas's char offsets in metadata already let it locate a fact's section.

findings.statement: Causal links between facts are extracted by default (server-only setting). Semantic links are created at retain for pairs at or above cosine 0.7, which sets graph density and is not retroactive. The default graph retriever, link_expansion, expands from semantic seeds through entity co-occurrence, semantic kNN and causal links.
findings.quote: Fast graph expansion from semantic seeds via entity co-occurrence, semantic kNN, and causal links.
findings.atlas_today: Defaults: causal links on, semantic link threshold 0.7 (calibrated for another embedding model).
findings.opportunity: Keep causal links on. Multi-hop recall rides on entity, semantic and causal links, so entity identity and semantic-link calibration are what to work on (findings above).

findings.topic: Metadata routing: only extraction moves, consolidation stays on the primary
findings.statement: Metadata routing chooses the member that extracts each item. The choice is not stored, and reprocessing replays the original metadata. Recall, reflect, consolidation, mental-model refresh and dry-run extraction stay on the primary LLM. Each operation can have its own chain, including CONSOLIDATION.
findings.quote: Each operation can define its own members + strategy with the `RETAIN` / `REFLECT` / `CONSOLIDATION` / `MENTAL_MODEL_REFRESH` prefix
findings.atlas_today: ATLAS_RETAIN_EXTRACTOR=minimax adds extractor: minimax to item metadata. docs/decisions.md already notes that consolidation of those facts still spends the ChatGPT (primary) quota, uncounted by Atlas.
findings.opportunity: Configure a HINDSIGHT_API_CONSOLIDATION_LLM_* chain on MiniMax (or count consolidation against codex). Note that dry-run extract tests the primary, not the routed member.

findings.statement: Consolidation runs automatically after retain, delete and update (enable_auto_consolidation, per bank). It sends 8 facts per LLM call (per bank) and handles at most 100 memories per round before re-queuing (per bank). Mental-model refreshes run only on the final round. Source facts in the prompt are capped at 4096 tokens in total and 256 per observation (per bank). Near-duplicate observations at cosine ≥ 0.97 go to a merge-or-keep LLM call (server).
findings.quote: When the limit is reached, the job yields its worker slot and re-queues itself so other banks get fair scheduling. Mental model refreshes only run on the final round.
findings.atlas_today: All defaults. Mental models refresh on a daily cron with refresh_after_consolidation false, so the final-round coupling does not apply to them.
findings.opportunity: During a bulk backfill, consider enable_auto_consolidation false, then an explicit consolidate (as replay banks already do), so consolidation sees whole filings rather than partial ones. Raise the per-observation source-fact cap if observations about one company draw on many filings.

findings.statement: max_observations_per_scope (default -1, unlimited; per bank) caps observations per tag scope. At the cap, consolidation only updates or deletes. Untagged observations are exempt. Scopes can be per_tag, all_combinations or an explicit list (observation_scopes), but this page only names them.
findings.quote: Applies per tag scope (e.g., per-tag when using `per_tag` observation scopes).
findings.atlas_today: Unlimited. Documents carry observation_scopes null (upsert/09-get-document recording), so the server's default scoping of company/theme tags applies, which this page does not document.
findings.opportunity: Find out in retain.md or observations.md how Atlas's company:/theme: tags group consolidation. Per-company observation scopes would keep observations company-grounded.

findings.statement: retain_mission is added to the extraction prompt next to the built-in rules and narrows focus without replacing them; it is ignored in chunks mode. Custom mode with retain_custom_instructions replaces the selectivity rules but keeps output format, temporal handling and coreference resolution.
findings.quote: The mission is injected into the extraction prompt alongside the built-in rules — it narrows focus without replacing the underlying logic.
findings.atlas_today: retain_mission is set (economically material facts: capacity, supply agreements, customer dependencies, ...). No custom instructions.
findings.opportunity: Keep the mission approach. Add naming the counterparty company in supplier/customer facts, and naming the filer rather than 'we', so that entity links form.

findings.statement: Extracted facts carry when/where/who/why. With HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_OPTIONAL_FACT_DIMENSIONS false (the default, server-only), the model must fill them. Under a strict schema it may then write a date the text gave for something else.
findings.quote: the nearest plausible one is a date the text stated about something else
findings.atlas_today: Default. Atlas sends timestamp = available_at, recorded as retain_params.event_date. LLM_STRICT_SCHEMA is not set.
findings.opportunity: Mostly none. If wrong dates show up on filing facts (filings state many dates), try optional dimensions, and LLM_SUPPORTS_STRING_PATTERN if the backend accepts `pattern`.

findings.topic: Dry-run extraction for testing intake settings
findings.statement: HINDSIGHT_API_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_EXTRACT (default true) exposes POST /banks/{bank_id}/memories/dry-run-extract. It runs extraction with a real LLM call and stores nothing.
findings.quote: Runs extraction only — makes a real LLM call but stores nothing.
findings.atlas_today: Not used.
findings.opportunity: A cheap harness for comparing modes, missions, strategies and chunk sizes on recorded filing sections and transcripts without polluting the research bank. It uses the primary LLM, not metadata routes.

contradictions: The HINDSIGHT_API_STORE_DOCUMENT_TEXT row in the Retain table says "Hierarchical — overridable per bank via the [config API]", but the "Skip storing raw document text" section says "This is a static, server-level setting and cannot be overridden per bank." The recordings (research_template/03-imported-config.json and the template schema) list store_document_text in the per-bank resolved config, so per-bank looks real in 0.10.1, though setting it per bank was not exercised.

The Hierarchical Configuration 'Security Model' lists 'retrieval settings' among static, server-only fields. Yet the Recall budget mapping and Recall pipeline stages sections, the bank-template schema and the resolved config all make recall budgets and the four retrieval arms hierarchical (per bank).

The Security Model's list of configurable fields names only a few retain and observation fields, while the template schema and resolved config expose many more per-bank fields (entity_labels, retain_strategies, consolidation_* and others). The list is incomplete rather than wrong.

Atlas docs disagree on which server Atlas uses: AGENTS.md says retains on MiniMax use 'the shared Hindsight', while docs/decisions.md (line 8) describes a 'dedicated Atlas Hindsight' distinct from the shared release. This matters for which server env the server-wide recommendations here (query prefix, gates, fail-on-error, consolidation chain) target.
not_covered: retain.md, api/retain.md and api/memory-banks.md: entity_labels format, the RetainContent.entities and resolve_entities item fields, update_mode, what occurred_start/occurred_end/mentioned_at mean, and whether `context` is repeated into each chunk's extraction prompt.
How a long item is split into chunks (sentence or paragraph boundaries, overlap): this page gives only the size and says nothing about overlap.

observation_scopes: which values exist and what the default is when it is null, i.e. how Atlas's company:/theme: tags group consolidation. This page only names per_tag, all_combinations and explicit lists.

The production cluster's Hindsight env (home-ops): I read only compose.yaml and spikes/hindsight/compose.yaml, so whether the cluster sets EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_PREFIX, entity thresholds or FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS is unverified.
docs/research/extraction-bakeoff.md (earlier measurements of modes and models): not re-read.

Lines 330–560 (LLM provider examples), 1019–1136 (embedding provider examples), 1245–1555 (reranker chain, auth, server, egress), 2035–2240 (file processing and storage) and 2609–2764 (observability): searched for intake terms, not read line by line.

result.summary:
I read configuration.md for everything that shapes what recall and reflect return. Recall runs four arms (semantic, BM25, graph, temporal) and fuses them with RRF. The top 300 candidates go to a reranker, then a linear 365-day recency nudge is applied. budget (low/mid/high = 100/300/1000 items per arm per fact type, set per bank) sets how wide retrieval searches. It does not set how many results come back. Most ranking knobs are server-only: the similarity thresholds, recency, strategy boosts, the reranker chain and BM25. Per bank Atlas can switch arms on or off, change the budget mapping, and set reflect's internal recall (chunk and fact token budgets), source facts, default options and consolidation batch size. Per mental model it can set exclude_mental_models, include_chunks, recall_max_tokens, keep_trace and mode.

Main risks for Atlas:
- All five similarity gates are calibrated for bge-small, but Atlas embeds with qwen3-embedding-0.6b.
- There is no rrf fail-open, so a rerank outage fails every recall.
- Native BM25 has no IDF and a 16-term cap.
- Reflect and the mental models read raw chunks (citations Atlas cannot resolve), get no source facts, may read each other, run at temperature 0.9 and keep no trace.
- Consolidation always runs on the primary LLM. Atlas's per-bank lever is consolidation_llm_batch_size (default 8 facts per call). Near-duplicate observations add extra one-by-one merge calls.

findings.statement: The five embedding gates (semantic 0.3, graph seed 0.3, temporal 0.1, semantic-link creation 0.7, observation dedup 0.97) are calibrated for BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5. The docs say to recalibrate all five when the embedding model changes. Atlas embeds with qwen3-embedding-0.6b, so every gate that admits candidates to recall, builds the semantic graph or dedups observations is uncalibrated for Atlas's corpus.
findings.quote: Their defaults preserve the behavior calibrated for `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`.
findings.atlas_today: Uses qwen3-embedding-0.6b (compose.yaml: `HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_OPENAI_MODEL: qwen3-embedding-0.6b`, the same as the cluster per its comment) with every threshold at its default. No calibration has been done.
findings.opportunity: Measure read-only how qwen3 cosine similarities are distributed on Atlas's own facts and queries (recall traces), then propose threshold values to the owner. Raising or lowering SEMANTIC_MIN_SIMILARITY and SEMANTIC_LINK_MIN_SIMILARITY changes what the reading index can return and how dense the graph is. The link threshold is not retroactive.

findings.statement: The request budget (low/mid/high, default mid) maps to a thinking_budget used by every retrieval arm. Under the default fixed function it is 100/300/1000 items per arm per fact type, independent of max_tokens. It sets how wide retrieval searches before fusion, not how many results are returned. The mapping is per bank (recall_budget_function, recall_budget_fixed_*, adaptive ratios, min/max are all in BankTemplateConfig). The reranker cap can be overridden per budget level server-side.
findings.quote: Items per retrieval method per fact type when `budget=mid` and function is `fixed`. | `300`
findings.atlas_today: Every recall uses the default `budget="mid"` (gateway.recall signature `budget: Budget = "mid"`; research RecallRequest default mid). Pointer recalls pass no budget, max_tokens or types.
findings.opportunity: Try budget=high on the Scout's theme-wide pointer recalls. They make no LLM call, so they cost nothing against the 40-operation budget. With the reranker cap at 300, wider arms mainly change which candidates survive RRF to be reranked. Compare pointer sets at mid and high on the pilot question.

findings.topic: fusion, reranker cap and strategy boosts
findings.statement: Candidates from the four arms are fused by RRF. Only the top HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_MAX_CANDIDATES (300) are reranked, and RRF pre-filters the rest. There is no per-arm cap by default. RECALL_STRATEGY_BOOSTS (server, empty by default) can favour an arm, e.g. graph:low/medium/high, both before the cap and after reranking.
findings.quote: The boost is applied in two places: before the reranker cap (so favoured candidates survive the `HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_MAX_CANDIDATES` budget) and after reranking (to nudge them up the final order)
findings.atlas_today: No boosts. Server defaults on the shared Hindsight (the cluster's env is not in this repo).
findings.opportunity: For multi-hop supply-chain reading, `graph:low` would keep graph-arm hits (company B reached through an entity that co-occurs in A's facts) from being cut before reranking. Only the owner can set it, and it affects every bank on the shared server.

findings.statement: By default a failing reranker fails the recall. A failover chain ending in `rrf` makes recall fail open and return the fusion order. Members are tried in order on every request, with no circuit breaker. Scores are not comparable across providers.
findings.quote: Ending the chain with `rrf` makes recall **fail open**: results come back in the order
findings.atlas_today: compose.yaml uses `HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_PROVIDER: litellm` with model `rerank` and no fallback member. A LiteLLM rerank outage fails every Scout pointer recall (recorded as pointer_recall_failed) and every /memory/recall.
findings.opportunity: Ask the owner to add `HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_1_PROVIDER=rrf` to the shared server, so a rerank outage degrades ranking quality instead of losing all pointers.

findings.statement: During reranking, a memory's age adds a small freshness adjustment to its final rank. The default is linear decay from today to a floor at 365 days (exponential with a 90-day half-life, or none, are the alternatives). The docs do not say which timestamp counts as the age, how large the adjustment is, or whether query_timestamp replaces 'today'.
findings.quote: `linear` (default) decays in a straight line from full freshness (today) to a floor reached at `HINDSIGHT_API_RECENCY_DECAY_LINEAR_WINDOW_DAYS`.
findings.atlas_today: Not considered. Pointer rank is taken as Hindsight returns it (pointer weight = 1/rank).
findings.opportunity: Facts from recent filings get a slight edge, which is mostly desirable. For replay banks at a past cutoff, 'today' is the real date, so recency may rank replayed facts differently from production at that time. Note this as a replay-comparability caveat rather than act on it.

findings.statement: The default text search is native Postgres (english dictionary). Native ranking has no IDF and matches are OR-joined. Queries over 16 terms are trimmed to the 16 most selective terms (lowest document frequency).
findings.quote: because native ranking has no IDF and re-ranks every match
findings.atlas_today: Scout queries, the round's question and bear-checklist items go to recall as written, and the arm is on.
findings.opportunity: Keep pointer-recall queries short and specific: product, layer and company terms, not long sentences. In a photonics bank, common words like 'optical' score like rare ones under a ranking with no IDF.

findings.statement: The only graph retriever is link_expansion. It expands from semantic seeds (cosine >= GRAPH_SEED_MIN_SIMILARITY 0.3) through entity co-occurrence, semantic kNN links (created at retain at cosine >= 0.7) and causal links, with at most 200 targets per entity and a 10 s timeout. Its quality depends on entity resolution at retain time.
findings.quote: Fast graph expansion from semantic seeds via entity co-occurrence, semantic kNN, and causal links. Target latency under 100ms.
findings.atlas_today: The graph arm is on. The template sets no entity_labels. Theme-wide any_strict scoping lets the graph cross companies inside the theme.
findings.opportunity: Multi-hop only works when name variants of a company (legal name, short name, ticker) resolve to one entity. Consider per-bank entity_labels or passing entities at retain for universe companies, and check entity merges in the research bank.

findings.statement: The temporal arm runs on a date constraint parsed from the query text (dateparser; auto-detecting languages is costly) with a 0.1 similarity floor. It adds candidates and filters nothing out. The feature matrix observed that a temporal window is not a hard filter.
findings.quote: a 2024 window still returned 7 of 14 results dated 2026, some ranked first
findings.atlas_today: Atlas applies its own as-of cutoff to pointers (none for a version available after as_of) and never relies on Hindsight's temporal filtering.
findings.opportunity: Keep the Atlas-side cutoff. Leave query dates like 'FY2026' in the query text when the question is period-bound, since that is what activates the arm.

findings.statement: API recall queries longer than 500 tokens are rejected with HTTP 400. Internal recalls (reflect, consolidation, MCP) are truncated instead.
findings.quote: API requests exceeding this limit are rejected with HTTP 400
findings.atlas_today: Scout queries are short. A long investigation question passed straight to recall could hit the limit.
findings.opportunity: Guard or trim question-length recall queries on Atlas's side so a long question does not turn into a failed pointer recall.

findings.topic: reflect internal recall: chunks and fact budget
findings.statement: Reflect's recall tool (also used by mental-model refresh) returns raw chunk text by default (RECALL_INCLUDE_CHUNKS true, 1000 tokens) alongside 2048 tokens of facts. These are set per bank, and per mental model via trigger.include_chunks, recall_max_tokens and recall_chunks_max_tokens. An explicit request from the reflect model wins.
findings.quote: Whether the internal recall returns raw chunk text alongside facts. Set `false` to skip chunks and save prompt budget.
findings.atlas_today: Defaults. The template sets neither recall_include_chunks nor any trigger recall fields. The feature matrix notes that chunk-sourced reflect content cannot be resolved and is labelled unverified.
findings.opportunity: For the mental models and reflect jobs, set include_chunks false and raise recall_max_tokens (e.g. 4096) so syntheses rest on memories Atlas can resolve to Source Version sections. Measure how the share of resolved citations changes.

findings.statement: By default reflect's search_observations tool returns observations without the world facts behind them (REFLECT_SOURCE_FACTS_MAX_TOKENS -1). 0 means unlimited, >0 sets a budget. It is per bank (reflect_source_facts_max_tokens). The search_observations budget defaults to 5000 tokens and can be changed through reflect_default_options.
findings.quote: `-1` disables source facts (default), `0` enables with no limit, `>0` enables with a token budget.
findings.atlas_today: Default (-1). Atlas resolves an observation through source_memory_ids after the fact, but the reflect model reasons from observation text alone.
findings.opportunity: Set reflect_source_facts_max_tokens (e.g. 2000–4000) in the template so reflect and mental models see the grounding facts. This fits the reflect_mission's 'distinguish factual statements'. Consider reflect_search_observations_include_entities false to win back context.

findings.topic: mental models read other mental models
findings.statement: The mental-model trigger's exclude_mental_models defaults to false, so a refresh may call search_mental_models and read other mental models' content. Other trigger fields: fact_types (default all), mode full|delta (default full), keep_trace (default false; the only way to see how a cron refresh reached its result).
findings.quote: If true, exclude all mental models from the reflect loop (skip search_mental_models tool).
findings.atlas_today: configs/hindsight/bank-template.json sets only refresh_after_consolidation false, refresh_cron, min_refresh_interval_seconds and max_tokens. Theme status and Bottlenecks can therefore cite each other's syntheses, which Atlas cannot resolve to a Source Version.
findings.opportunity: Add `exclude_mental_models: true` and `keep_trace: true` to both models' triggers (a template version bump). That keeps each model grounded in memories and records retrieved-vs-used counts for review.

findings.statement: Reflect allows at most 10 tool iterations and 100000 accumulated context tokens before forcing a synthesis, and has a 300 s wall timeout (HTTP 504). The per-call reflect LLM timeout defaults to 30 s. Final synthesis output is uncapped unless REFLECT_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS is set.
findings.quote: | `HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_WALL_TIMEOUT` | Wall-clock timeout in seconds for the entire reflect operation. If exceeded, the request returns HTTP 504. | `300` |
findings.atlas_today: The gateway's `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 300.0` equals the server wall timeout, so a long reflect can race Atlas's client timeout against Hindsight's 504. Compose raises the reflect LLM timeout to 300.
findings.opportunity: Set the client timeout a little above 300 s, so a slow reflect surfaces as Hindsight's 504 (a classified failure) rather than a client timeout. Treat 504 as retryable without spending more budget than needed.

findings.statement: The reflect 'thinking' step samples at temperature 0.9 by default, against 0.1 for retain and 0.0 for consolidation. It is server-level only.
findings.quote: Temperature for the reflect "thinking" step. Number in `[0.0, 2.0]` or `none` to omit. Overrides `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_TEMPERATURE`. | `0.9` |
findings.atlas_today: Default. The daily mental models (mode full) are regenerated from scratch at 0.9, so content can change day to day without new evidence. Atlas skips refreshes that are not stale.
findings.opportunity: Ask the owner for a lower REFLECT (or MENTAL_MODEL_REFRESH extra_body) temperature, or use trigger mode delta so unchanged sections stay byte-for-byte. Either makes mental-model history diffs mean new evidence rather than sampling noise.

findings.topic: per-operation LLM routing and what metadata routing leaves on the primary
findings.statement: Retain, reflect, consolidation and mental-model refresh each have an LLM group and an optional chain (refresh inherits reflect). Metadata routing chooses only the retain extractor. Recall uses no LLM.
findings.quote: recall, reflect, consolidation, mental-model refresh and dry-run extraction all continue to use the primary LLM
findings.atlas_today: Atlas knows this (decisions.md: consolidation of MiniMax-extracted facts still spends the ChatGPT quota, uncounted).
findings.opportunity: The owner could set HINDSIGHT_API_CONSOLIDATION_LLM_* (or a CONSOLIDATION chain) on the shared server to take consolidation off the 40-operations-per-5h primary. MENTAL_MODEL_REFRESH_LLM_* could likewise go to a cheap no-think model. Atlas cannot set either itself.

findings.topic: consolidation batch size (cost lever Atlas owns)
findings.statement: Consolidation sends 8 facts per LLM call by default (per bank). Higher values mean fewer calls but larger prompts. Each new or updated observation at cosine >= 0.97 to an existing one adds a one-by-one merge-or-keep LLM call. Rounds handle at most 100 memories, and mental-model refreshes run only on the final round.
findings.quote: Number of facts sent to the LLM in a single consolidation call. Higher values reduce LLM calls and improve throughput at the cost of larger prompts.
findings.atlas_today: Default 8 (not in the template).
findings.opportunity: Raise consolidation_llm_batch_size in the template (e.g. 16–24) to cut the primary-LLM calls consolidation spends per retained section. Check observation quality on a sample before keeping it.

findings.statement: WORKER_MAX_SLOTS defaults to 10, with 2 reserved for consolidation. Reservations are floors, not caps. Only one consolidation runs per bank at a time, whatever the slots. The poller claims queued work every 500 ms, regardless of the sweep intervals.
findings.quote: Consolidation's bank-serialization constraint (no two consolidation tasks for the same bank concurrently) is preserved regardless of which pool claims the slot.
findings.atlas_today: Local compose uses 4 slots with LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT 2. Everything goes into one research bank, so its consolidation drains serially.
findings.opportunity: After a backfill burst, observations (part of the reading index) lag world facts until the bank's single consolidation chain drains. Pointer recalls taken during a backlog miss new observations. Consider waiting for consolidation to drain (operations API) before a scheduled investigation.

findings.statement: Per bank, the BM25, temporal, graph and reranking stages can each be switched off (semantic always runs). Without reranking, recall returns the RRF order. These are in the recorded BankTemplateConfig.
findings.quote: `false` returns the RRF-fused ordering directly — faster, but less precise.
findings.atlas_today: All on (defaults).
findings.opportunity: None for the research bank. The toggles are useful in evaluation banks to measure each arm's contribution to pointer quality (ablation), without touching production.

result.summary:
Atlas uses only a thin slice of Hindsight's API. On recall it sends query, budget=mid and strict OR tags. It keeps each result's text, document_id, metadata, dates and tags. It drops scores, the entities map (with entity IDs, which recall returns by default), chunks, source facts and trace. It never sets max_tokens (default 4096), so every pointer recall holds about 10 to 14 memories. On retain it sends no entities, observation_scopes, strategy or operation_id. Reflect runs at the server default budget 'low'.

Biggest gap for multi-hop supply-chain work: GET /memories/list?entity_id= is an exhaustive reverse lookup from an entity to every fact that mentions it. It can be filtered by tags and by time window, and each fact carries document_id plus Atlas metadata, so each one points to a section. That gives a deterministic, as-of-filterable company-to-company hop that ranked, unfiltered recall cannot. It needs stable entities, but the recordings show one company split into 'Aurora Optics' and 'Aurora Optics Inc.'. Retain `entities` with resolve_entities=false would fix that.

Second gap: under the default observation scope 'combined', observations form per exact tag set. Atlas tags every item with company, theme, source, doctype and form, so observations are split by form and source.

Also unused: include.source_facts (would replace Atlas's 1+N get_memory calls per observation), tag_groups (AND/NOT scopes), query_timestamp, min_scores, the entity co-occurrence graph, tags counts and bank stats. None of these has been recorded against 0.10.1.

findings.statement: GET /memories/list accepts entity_id, an exact reverse lookup over stored entity links. It can be combined with type, tags/tags_match and time_field+start_date/end_date, where the date range filters rather than ranks. Each returned fact carries document_id and metadata. So from one company it lists every fact naming it in any filing, including other companies' filings. Atlas never calls it, and drops the entity IDs that recall already returns.
findings.quote: so you can list an entity's evidence (e.g. its observations, with `type=observation`) without scanning every memory
findings.atlas_today: memories/list is used only with type=observation and document_id (gateway list_observations, document_memories). Entity IDs from recall are discarded.
findings.opportunity: A deterministic, exhaustive, as-of-filterable company-to-company hop. Take the entity_id of a company named in a read filing, list its facts across the bank (tags/time filtered), and turn each fact's metadata.source_version_id/section_anchor into a reading pointer. That reaches suppliers and customers named in other filers' documents, which a theme-scoped top-k recall can miss.

findings.statement: Recall includes entities by default (include.entities default max_tokens 500). The response's entities map gives entity_id and canonical_name for every entity in the results, and the recordings show 17 to 21 entries per recall. Atlas's RecallResult keeps only `results`, and Memory has no entities field.
findings.quote:
class RecallResult(_Result):
    memories: list[Memory] = Field(validation_alias="results")
findings.atlas_today: Drops the per-result entity names and the response-level entity map, which is already paid for in every recall.
findings.opportunity: Keep the entity map so a pointer can carry the entity IDs it mentions. Those IDs feed memories/list?entity_id= and give the ranking of pointed companies an entity-level signal besides the section's company tag.

findings.statement: MemoryItem accepts `entities` (text, optional type), combined with the auto-extracted ones. With resolve_entities=false the names are taken literally. Atlas sends none, and the extractor's resolution split one company into two entities in the recorded recall: 'Aurora Optics' and 'Aurora Optics Inc.', with different entity_ids.
findings.quote: "canonical_name": "Aurora Optics Inc.",
findings.atlas_today: RetainItem has no entities field. Entity identity is left entirely to Hindsight's extractor.
findings.opportunity: Send the filer's canonical name, and Atlas-resolved universe/counterparty names found in the section, as entities with resolve_entities=false. Then each company has one stable entity that entity_id listing, the entity graph and graph-arm recall can follow. Test first with POST /memories/dry-run-extract (no storage).

findings.topic: observation scopes fragmented by Atlas's tags
findings.statement: Per-item observation_scopes defaults to 'combined', a single consolidation pass with all of the item's tags together, and an observation scope is an exact tag set. Atlas tags every item with company, each theme, source, doctype and form, so observations form only among memories with identical tag sets. A company's 10-K facts and its 10-Q or transcript facts fall into different scopes. GET /observations/scopes enumerates the scopes with counts.
findings.quote: 'combined' (default) runs a single pass with all tags together.
findings.atlas_today: No observation_scopes sent. Tags from version_tags include source:, doctype: and form: alongside company: and theme:. POST /consolidate is sent as {} (no scopes).
findings.opportunity: Call GET /observations/scopes to measure fragmentation. Consider explicit scopes such as [["company:<id>"],["theme:<slug>"]] so observations synthesise across a company's filings and across the theme. Confirm the semantics against the observations page (lead's slice) first.

findings.statement: RecallRequest.max_tokens defaults to 4096 and bounds how much the result list holds. Atlas never sends it, so every pointer recall is capped (10 to 14 results in the recordings). budget is always 'mid'. Under the default fixed mapping, low/mid/high mean per-arm retrieval limits of 100/300/1000.
findings.quote: body: dict[str, JsonValue] = {"query": query, "budget": budget, **_scope_fields(scope)}
findings.atlas_today: Sends query, budget (mid by default) and tags only. The Scout's theme recall uses the defaults.
findings.opportunity: Raise max_tokens (and maybe budget=high) for the Scout's pointer recalls. Recall makes no LLM call, so more pointers per query cost latency only, and more of the theme's companies and sections get pointed at.

findings.statement: With include.source_facts, recall returns each observation's source_fact_ids and a source_facts map keyed by fact ID. The map values are full RecallResult objects (document_id, metadata, chunk_id), with source_facts_truncated set when the budget cut it. Atlas instead makes 1 + N GET /memories calls per observation. Not exercised in any recording: without the option, source_fact_ids is null on observations.
findings.quote: Source facts for observation-type results, keyed by fact ID
findings.atlas_today: ProvenanceResolver calls get_memory on the observation, then on each source memory.
findings.opportunity: Request include.source_facts={} on pointer and research recalls and resolve observations from the response. This saves HTTP calls per recall and lets the Scout record observation pointers without extra round trips. Verify against 0.10.1 first, because it is unrecorded.

findings.topic: no date filter in recall; as-of
findings.statement: Recall has no date filter: temporal_window only ranks, and the feature matrix confirmed that a 2024 window still returned 2026 results. query_timestamp anchors recency scoring. memories/list's time_field/start_date/end_date is a real filter. tag_groups support NOT, so tag-based period exclusion is possible.
findings.quote: Used as the query-time anchor for relative temporal expressions and recency scoring.
findings.atlas_today: No query_timestamp. as_of is enforced after recall by dropping pointers to versions available after as_of, so those memories still use up recall slots.
findings.opportunity: Send query_timestamp=as_of for investigations and replays. For hard as-of scoping, either use memories/list with a time window (exhaustive), or tag items with an availability period and exclude later periods with a tag_groups NOT leaf.

findings.topic: scope is a union; tag_groups unused
findings.statement: Atlas builds one tag list of company: and theme: tags with any_strict, which is an OR. Hindsight's tag_groups allow AND/OR/NOT trees of leaves, so scopes like company AND form:10-K or theme AND NOT source:tradingview become possible.
findings.quote: tags = [f"company:{c}" for c in company_ids] + [f"theme:{t}" for t in theme_ids]
findings.atlas_today: A scope of company_ids and theme_ids returns memories of any of them (union). No form/source/doctype scoping, although those tags are written at retain.
findings.opportunity: Use tag_groups with strict leaves (resolve='exact') to target recall at document families, such as periodic reports only or transcripts only, or at a company within a theme. This gives the Skeptic's per-company checklist recalls and the Investigators sharper pointers.

findings.statement: Every recall result carries scores (final, reranker, semantic, keyword). min_scores can set post-ranking floors on reranker/final that every returned result is guaranteed to clear. The schema warns that reranker scores are not calibrated across queries. Atlas keeps only the list order.
findings.quote: post-ranking filters applied to every scored result, so those floors *are* guaranteed by each result returned
findings.atlas_today: Pointer weight is 1/rank (`for rank, memory in enumerate(response.memories, start=1):`). Scores are not parsed.
findings.opportunity: Store scores.final/reranker on each reading pointer, and weight pointed companies by relevance instead of rank alone. Optionally set a min_scores.final floor so weak queries add no pointers.

findings.statement: types filters fact types (world, experience, observation). prefer_observations drops raw facts that a returned observation was consolidated from, and backfills the freed slots. Atlas sends neither, so results mix observations, which need the two-hop resolution, with facts that duplicate them.
findings.quote: When recalling raw facts ('world'/'experience') together with 'observation', drop any raw fact that an observation in the results was consolidated from
findings.atlas_today: All types, no dedup.
findings.opportunity: For pointer recalls, either types=["world"] (each hit carries document_id and metadata inline, so it is a direct section pointer) or prefer_observations=true with include.source_facts, so slots are not spent on duplicates.

findings.statement: Each fact carries chunk_id. include.chunks returns the chunk text keyed by chunk_id, and GET /chunks/{chunk_id} returns chunk_text and chunk_index. Atlas parses chunk_id but nothing uses it. It points the Investigator at the section, then picks the window that best matches the memory text.
findings.quote: chunk_id: str | None = None
findings.atlas_today: chunk_id parsed, unused. No chunk reads.
findings.opportunity: Use the fact's chunk (at most retain_chunk_size, 3000 chars by default) to place a pointer inside a long section exactly, instead of a best-match window. The docs do not say whether chunk_text is a verbatim substring of the retained content, so check before relying on offsets.

findings.statement: GET /entities/graph returns entity nodes (with mention counts) and co-occurrence edges (with weight and lastCooccurred). It is bank-wide, with limit and min_count only and no tag filter. GET /entities lists entities by mention count. The entity observations returned with them are deprecated and empty.
findings.quote: Return a graph of entities (nodes) and their co-occurrences (edges) for visualization.
findings.atlas_today: Never called.
findings.opportunity: Use it as a candidate-pair index: universe company or counterparty entities that co-occur with a seed company's entity are companies to read next, and the duplicates it shows reveal entity fragmentation. It stays a reading pointer only, since co-mention forms no edge under Atlas's rules.

findings.statement: Atlas's reflect sends only query, tags scope, include.facts and an optional response_schema. budget is left at the schema default 'low' and max_tokens at 4096. Mental models are not excluded, so a reflect may lean on the Theme status/Bottlenecks models, whose content is not resolved like memories. fact_types, tag_groups and include.tool_calls are unused.
findings.quote: body: dict[str, Any] = {"query": query, **_scope_fields(scope)}
findings.atlas_today: Default budget (low). Mental models allowed. No trace.
findings.opportunity: Send budget explicitly (mid/high for research questions). Consider exclude_mental_models=true, or exclude_mental_model_ids, when citations must resolve to Source Versions. Use include.tool_calls when diagnosing thin answers.

findings.opportunity: Watch pending and failed consolidation (facts never consolidated never appear as observations), and recover failed ones. Compare a mental model's last_memory_seen_at (dropped today) with last_memory_write_at.

findings.quote: List all unique tags in a memory bank with usage counts. Supports wildcard search using '*'
findings.atlas_today: Never called.
findings.opportunity: A cheap memory-coverage check per company, form or source for the Theme explorer's coverage gaps and for deciding which companies' filings to retain next.

findings.quote: Get the full history of an observation, with each change's source facts resolved to their text.
findings.atlas_today: Never called.

findings.quote: Re-submitting with the same operation_id returns the original operation and creates no new work, so retrying after a lost or timed-out acknowledgement will not enqueue a duplicate.

result.summary:
Reflect is an agentic loop (≤10 iterations) over four tools, used in this order: mental models first, then observations, then raw-fact recall, plus expand. budget (low default/mid/high) sets how deep it searches. max_tokens caps only the final answer. response_schema adds a second extraction pass. based_on lists cited memories, models and directives, all validated against what was retrieved. A mental model is a stored reflect answer: reading it is free, and refreshing it costs one full reflect loop. Refreshes are skipped at no cost when nothing in the model's scope changed. Knowledge pages are mental models with preset defaults (delta mode, observations only, exclude sibling models, refresh after consolidation) plus a folder tree and page search. They are not part of bank templates.

Five things matter most for Atlas. (1) Its reflects are scoped any_strict and its two models carry no tags, so no Atlas reflect can see either model. (2) The gateway sends no budget, so every reflect runs at the shallow `low` level. (3) The models can read each other (exclude_mental_models is unset), and any citation of a model is silently dropped. (4) Grounding facts behind observations are off by default. (5) Refreshes and reflects never count against the codex budget, and Hindsight's own cron runs outside Atlas's queue. Adding per-company and per-layer models is affordable (realistically 5-10 refreshes a day) once those are fixed. Per-layer scoping can use tag_groups over company tags.

findings.topic: reflect scope hides Atlas's mental models
findings.statement: With non-empty tags and any_strict/all_strict, reflect's search_mental_models sees only mental models whose tags match. Atlas scopes every reflect any_strict on company:/theme: tags and its two models are untagged, so no Atlas reflect ever consults Theme status or Bottlenecks. Untagged directives still apply.
findings.quote: | Non-empty `tags`, `any_strict` or `all_strict` | Matching tagged data only | Matching tagged models only | Matching tagged directives plus untagged/global directives |
findings.atlas_today: SCOPE_MATCH = "any_strict" in backend/atlas/research/service.py; decisions.md 2026-09-29: "Both have `max_tokens` 2048, no tags (the bank holds only Atlas-retained, tagged material)".
findings.opportunity: Decide deliberately. Either tag both models theme:photonics, so a theme-scoped reflect sees them while refresh still reads the same theme-tagged memories through all_strict. Or keep them hidden on purpose, because an answer built on a model cites based_on.mental_models, which Atlas cannot resolve to a Source Version section.

findings.statement: budget controls how deeply the reflect agent explores. `low` is the default and is a shallow search. Only `high` explores all knowledge levels and tries several query variations to find indirect connections. The docs give no iteration or token figures per level.
findings.quote: At `low`, the agent does a shallow search optimized for speed. At `mid`, it checks multiple sources when the question warrants it. At `high`, it performs deep exploration across all knowledge levels and may use multiple query variations to find indirect connections.
findings.atlas_today: backend/atlas/hindsight/gateway.py reflect sends no budget: `body: dict[str, Any] = {"query": query, **_scope_fields(scope)}`, so every Atlas reflect runs at `low`.
findings.opportunity: Add budget to ReflectRequest and the gateway. Default to mid, and use high for multi-hop supply-chain questions and the replay question set. Measure token use from the response's usage field.

findings.statement: Reflect is an agentic tool loop: search_mental_models first, then search_observations, then recall over raw facts as the fallback, plus expand for more context, then done. It runs at most 10 iterations, must gather evidence before it answers, and only IDs it actually retrieved can be cited. A stale model does not short-circuit the loop, and a stale observation is checked against the raw facts.
findings.quote: 2. **Uses hierarchical retrieval** — Checks mental models first, then observations, then raw facts
findings.atlas_today: Atlas uses reflect only for the reflect job and for mental-model refreshes. Its scope excludes the models (see the first finding), so in practice its reflects start at observations.
findings.opportunity: Expect reflect citations to be mostly observations, as the spike observed. That keeps the two-hop resolution through source_memory_ids central.

findings.statement: By default, search_observations returns only the consolidated observation text. With HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_SOURCE_FACTS_MAX_TOKENS set (or the per-bank reflect_source_facts_max_tokens field in the template schema), it also returns the world facts each observation rests on.
findings.quote: if `HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_SOURCE_FACTS_MAX_TOKENS` is enabled — off by default — observation search also returns each observation's grounding facts.
findings.atlas_today: Not set in configs/hindsight/bank-template.json.
findings.opportunity: Set reflect_source_facts_max_tokens in the template's bank section. Reflect and refreshes would then see the exact figures and periods behind each belief, which supports the 'Never fabricate figures' directive, and could cite world facts that resolve in one hop. The cost is more context tokens per reflect.

findings.statement: Unless exclude_mental_models is set, a mental model's refresh can synthesise from sibling models. Knowledge pages turn this off by default to prevent a feedback loop in which one wrong claim spreads across documents.
findings.quote: | `exclude_mental_models: true` | A page never reflects on sibling pages. Without this, pages would cite each other and drift into a feedback loop where one wrong claim propagates across the knowledge base. |
findings.atlas_today: Both template models leave exclude_mental_models unset (false). Atlas's parser drops the 'mental-models' group from based_on (`_NON_MEMORY_BASED_ON = frozenset({"directives", "mental-models"})` in backend/atlas/hindsight/models.py), so a citation of a sibling model disappears silently.
findings.opportunity: Add "exclude_mental_models": true to both triggers, and to any future per-company or per-layer model.

findings.statement: A mental-model refresh is a full reflect run: retrieval plus the agentic loop of up to 10 iterations, plus one structured-output pass if the trigger has a schema. A dry run costs the same. Reading a model is only a database read.
findings.quote: A refresh is a full reflect run: retrieval plus an agentic LLM loop.
findings.atlas_today: Two models are refreshed daily on Hindsight's 06:00 cron. Atlas's job at 06:30 usually skips with min_interval or not_stale. The Scout reads Bottlenecks as a free GET.
findings.opportunity: Price each additional model at one reflect per day on which its scope changed. In the spike, one reflect took about 24-28 s and about 10.6k input and 1.9k output tokens on a tiny bank.

findings.statement: Both automatic triggers check whether any memory in the model's resolved scope (tags, tags_match, tag_groups, fact_types) is newer than its last refresh, and skip with no LLM call if none is. Memories not yet consolidated count as new. Deletions do not.
findings.quote: Both automatic triggers run the same check before spending an LLM call: **is there a memory in this model's resolved scope newer than its last refresh?**
findings.atlas_today: Atlas reads is_stale and skips not_stale models. Its models are untagged, so their scope is the whole bank and any retain makes them stale.
findings.opportunity: Narrowly scoped models (per company) are free on days without new filings, which makes many small models cheap.

findings.statement: Atlas's codex budget counts units only from hindsight_operation rows (retain/reprocess batches) and replay operations. reflect and refresh_mental_model jobs are held when the window is spent but never add a unit, and Hindsight's own refresh_cron runs outside Atlas's queue.
findings.quote: "SELECT h.id AS source_id, 1 AS units FROM hindsight_operation h"
findings.atlas_today: refresh.py: "Hindsight's own `refresh_cron` (06:00 UTC in the template) is gated by the same minimum". decisions.md accepts that the cron is not pause-aware. With 2 models the gap is small.
findings.opportunity: Before adding models, record one codex unit per reflect and per submitted refresh. Also consider letting Atlas's job be the only scheduler: give Hindsight a far-off cron and refresh through Atlas, so refreshes are counted and pausable.

findings.topic: structured output on a mental model
findings.statement: trigger.response_schema makes every refresh store a structured_output next to the markdown, extracted from the final stored document. If the extraction fails, the refresh fails and the previous content is kept.
findings.quote: If a `response_schema` is configured but the structured extraction cannot be produced, the refresh **fails** rather than silently persisting content with no structured view.
findings.atlas_today: No response_schema on either model. The Scout gets Bottlenecks as quoted markdown (backend/atlas/discovery/service.py _gaps).
findings.opportunity: Give Bottlenecks a schema: constraints with layer, status confirmed/unconfirmed, missing_evidence[], and companies, using explicit *_known booleans because union types return 500. The Scout and the Theme explorer could then use structured gaps.

findings.topic: mental model tags and refresh scope
findings.statement: A tagged model's refresh reads with all_strict by default: a memory must carry every one of the model's tags, and untagged memories are excluded. trigger.tags_match or tag_groups override this. tag_groups are boolean expressions that replace flat tags entirely.
findings.quote: If the mental model has tags, that reflect call uses `all_strict` tag matching — meaning it will only read memories that carry **all** of the mental model's tags. Untagged memories are excluded.
findings.atlas_today: Every memory carries company:<uuid>, theme:<slug>, source:, doctype: and form: tags. There are no layer tags.
findings.opportunity: A per-company model tagged company:<uuid> reads exactly that company's memories. A per-layer model can use tag_groups (any) over the company: tags of the companies in that layer, without adding a layer tag at retain time. It then misses layer statements in other companies' filings.

findings.statement: delta mode edits a structured document with typed operations, copies untouched sections byte for byte, reads only memories created since the last refresh, and accumulates based_on across refreshes. It never writes a partial document. The docs suggest a periodic clear plus refresh to undo drift.
findings.quote: A delta refresh scopes its retrieval to memories created since the last refresh, so the LLM reads genuinely new information rather than re-reading the whole bank.
findings.atlas_today: Both models use the default, full mode, with fact_types unset (world, experience and observation).
findings.opportunity: Keep full mode for Bottlenecks, which has to re-judge every constraint each time. Consider delta with fact_types [observation] for long per-company models to cut cost, with a weekly clear plus refresh. Try it with dry-run-refresh first, which costs as much as a real refresh.

findings.statement: Directives affect only reflect, and so also mental-model refreshes. Untagged directives apply to every reflect. Tagged ones apply only when the request's tags match, unless apply_all_directives is true.
findings.quote: - **Untagged directives always apply**, on every `reflect`.
findings.atlas_today: Five untagged directives (cite evidence, say what's missing, never fabricate figures, flag source uncertainty, no trading orders) apply to every reflect and refresh. This matches the docs' guardrail use.
findings.opportunity: Tagged directives could add theme-specific rules, for example a theme:photonics rule that applies the second-source-and-pricing-power test, and they would load automatically on theme-scoped reflects.

findings.statement: reflect_mission and the disposition traits affect only reflect, and the mission goes into the system prompt. The docs describe the mission as a first-person identity narrative. Their Research Assistant preset is skepticism 4, literalism 3, empathy 3.
findings.quote: A first-person narrative that provides identity and framing context for `reflect`. The agent uses this to ground its reasoning and apply a consistent perspective.
findings.atlas_today: configs/hindsight/bank-template.json has an imperative mission ("Form source-grounded research syntheses. ... Seek disconfirmation."), skepticism 4, literalism 4, and empathy unset (3).
findings.opportunity: Rewrite the mission as an identity ("You are a supply-chain research analyst ..."). Consider empathy 1-2. Check the result with POST /prompts/preview {"operation":"reflect"}, which makes no LLM call.

findings.statement: Reflect's based_on (with include.facts) has memories (world, experience, observation; no document_id), mental_models and directives. A mental model's stored reflect_response.based_on is grouped by fact type instead, as recorded in 0.10.1.
findings.quote: - `memories` — a list of memory facts (world, experience, observation) that were retrieved and cited. Each item has `id`, `text`, `type`, `context`, `occurred_start`, and `occurred_end`.
findings.atlas_today: Atlas flattens both shapes (models.py _flatten_based_on, _memories_in_based_on) and resolves memories in two hops.
findings.opportunity: none

findings.statement: Observed in 0.10.1: reflect can put content from raw chunks into its answer without citing any memory ID for it.
findings.quote: Reflect can answer from raw chunks as well as facts (bake-off: a table figure absent from facts appeared in reflect output).
findings.atlas_today: Atlas checks each double-quoted passage against the archived text, but an unquoted figure that came from a chunk stays unverified.
findings.opportunity: For mental models, include_chunks: false on the trigger (or fact_types [observation], which removes the recall tool) keeps the content to citable memories.

findings.statement: A knowledge page is a mental model with preset defaults (delta, observations only, exclude sibling models, refresh after consolidation, max_tokens 4096), plus a folder tree and page search (BM25 plus vector, fused by RRF, no reranking). Pages are not in the bank-template manifest. The bank field knowledge_page_default_trigger can make new pages cron-driven.
findings.quote: A knowledge page *is* a [mental model](./mental-models). Same synthesis, same background refresh, same provenance.
findings.atlas_today: Not used (decisions.md: 'No knowledge pages in Phase 2').
findings.opportunity: Little gain over mental models with the same trigger fields. Pages would need their own API calls and a cron default, because their refresh_after_consolidation default breaks Atlas's no-runaway rule.

findings.statement: For every discovery, the Scout reads the current Bottlenecks content, whatever the investigation's as_of is.
findings.quote: gaps, gaps_source = self._gaps()
findings.atlas_today: _gaps() ignores as_of, so a back-dated investigation's Scout sees gaps synthesised from later filings. Replay banks import no models and are unaffected.
findings.opportunity: Skip the gaps when as_of is in the past, or use the history entry dated before as_of. The history endpoint keeps up to 50 previous versions.

findings.statement: By default an observation is scoped to all of a memory's tags combined. Atlas's memories carry company, theme, source, doctype and form tags and send no observation_scopes, so observations never merge across companies or across forms. Cross-company synthesis happens only inside a theme model's reflect.
findings.quote: By default, observations are scoped to all of a memory's tags combined.
findings.atlas_today: backend/atlas/retention/service.py version_tags adds company:, theme:, source:, doctype: and form:. There is no observation_scopes anywhere in backend/.
findings.opportunity: The lead owns observations. Note that a theme or layer model with fact_types [observation] would read only per-company, per-form beliefs.

findings.statement: A refresh that fails appends a history entry with kind refresh_failed, a failure_reason and previous_content null.
findings.quote: Those runs now append a failure record carrying the reason and the exception.
findings.atlas_today: MentalModelRevision in backend/atlas/hindsight/models.py ignores kind, so a failure record shows up as a revision with empty content.
findings.opportunity: Parse kind and failure_reason, and show failure records separately.

contradictions: Directive enforcement: api/memory-banks.md says directives are 'Strict — responses are rejected if violated', but reflect.md only says they 'must be followed exactly', and no rejection mechanism is documented anywhere.

Reflect trace tool names: api/reflect.md lists `lookup`, `recall`, `learn`, `expand`; reflect.md lists `search_mental_models`, `search_observations`, `recall`, `expand`, `done`. Neither was observed, because `trace` was null in the recording.

Atlas's bank_template.py docstring and decisions.md (2026-09-29) say 'an imported model defaults to `true`' for refresh_after_consolidation. The recorded template schema (bank_templates/01-schema.json) and api/mental-models.md give a default of false. The recorded export shows true only for a knowledge-page-backed model, and true is the knowledge-page default. Harmless, because Atlas sets false explicitly.

Mental-model based_on shape: the docs describe reflect_response as the 'Full reflect response including based_on provenance facts', which suggests reflect's {memories, mental_models, directives}. The 0.10.1 recording (mental_models/03-get.json) groups it by fact type instead (world, observation, opinion, experience, directives, mental-models). The recording wins.
api/bank-templates.md calls directive tags 'Tags for categorization', while api/memory-banks.md and api/reflect.md say tags decide when a directive applies.

decisions.md treats untagged models as harmless ('the bank holds only Atlas-retained, tagged material'), but with Atlas's any_strict scope the reflect docs make untagged models invisible to every Atlas reflect.
not_covered: How many iterations or tokens each reflect budget level (low/mid/high) means: not documented.
Which budget a mental-model refresh's internal reflect uses, and whether any trigger field sets it: not documented.
Whether recall returns mental models: only reflect.md's example claims it. The lead's recall pages should settle this.
Whether re-importing a template deletes mental models or directives the new template omits: not documented.
configuration.md (server defaults such as HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_SOURCE_FACTS_MAX_TOKENS and the mental-model history limits), monitoring and the LLM request log, MCP and SDK pages: not read.
Atlas's backend/atlas/mental_models/reads.py and the provenance resolver: not read beyond what the findings needed.

The per-company and per-layer cost estimates (about 5-10 refreshes a day for 21 models) are my inference from filing cadence and staleness gating, not measured. Token cost per refresh on the production bank is unknown; the spike used a tiny synthetic bank.

No live call was made, so none of the opportunities was verified against 0.10.1 (for example tag_groups on a mental-model trigger, reflect_source_facts_max_tokens, or exclude_mental_models taking effect).

result.summary:
The vendored changelog stops at 0.10.0. It has no 0.10.1 entry, and the repo disagrees with itself on whether the cluster runs 0.10.1 or 0.10.2. Several bugs that lost or corrupted memories were fixed by 0.10.0. These covered oversized documents losing content when split, chunk IDs colliding between banks, consolidation dropping items or writing only part of a batch, observations citing missing sources, and reprocess doing nothing. Atlas runs on a version with those fixes.

The biggest gaps Atlas still has:
(1) By default, a chunk that fails extraction still leaves the retain operation 'completed'. Atlas only catches sections with zero facts, so partial loss inside a long 10-K Item goes unseen. Fixing this takes a server-level setting (`FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS`), so it is the owner's call.
(2) Atlas passes no `entities` / `resolve_entities` on retain items. Hindsight's graph only links facts through shared entities, plus semantic and causal links between facts. There are no edges from one entity to another, so company-name variants that don't merge break the multi-hop expansion.
(3) Metadata routing changes only who extracts. Consolidation, reflect and mental-model refresh all stay on the primary Codex model, and that model's shared `auth.json` can break reflect while recall keeps working.
(4) Recall is sent with no `query_timestamp`, `prefer_observations` or `max_tokens`, and reflect never excludes mental models.

The docs say extraction needs no smart model but at least 65k output tokens. They give no guidance on mixing models across retain, consolidation and reflect.

findings.statement: Since 0.8.5, retain can be set to fail when any fact-extraction error occurs. By default (false), an operation in which some chunks failed extraction is still marked 'completed', so the facts those chunks would have produced vanish without notice. The setting is static and applies to the whole server.
findings.quote: | `HINDSIGHT_API_FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS` | When `true`, a retain operation that accumulated any fact-extraction errors is marked `failed`
findings.atlas_today: Atlas detects only sections with zero facts (reprocessed once, then marked `zero_fact`). A long Item section is many 3,000-char extraction chunks, and losing some of them is not detected.
findings.opportunity: Ask the owner to set HINDSIGHT_API_FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS=true on the shared server (it affects hermes too). Alternatively, Atlas could compare each section's memory count with its length to flag sections that yielded too few facts.

findings.statement: Entities are never linked to each other directly. They connect only by being attached to the same memory. Recall starts from semantic hits and expands through shared entities, precomputed semantic links between memories, and extracted causal links (causes/caused_by/enables/prevents). A supplier or customer direction exists only inside the fact text.
findings.quote: No. In Hindsight, entities (people, places, concepts, or classification labels) do not have direct arrows connecting them to one another.
findings.atlas_today: Atlas builds its own typed, directed Relationships from Assertions. Memory serves as the reading index (reading pointers).
findings.opportunity: Don't expect Hindsight's graph to stand in for supply-chain edges. Multi-hop recall works only to the extent that the same company resolves to the same entity across documents (see the entities finding).

findings.statement: Since 0.9.2, a retain item can carry `entities` (combined with the auto-extracted ones) and `resolve_entities`. When `resolve_entities` is false, the given names are taken literally. Separately, 0.9.2 stopped entity merges based only on history-matched names, and 0.9.0 improved deduplication within a batch.
findings.quote: Retain and update_memory can now optionally resolve entities via a dedicated flag, enabling more controlled entity handling.
findings.atlas_today: RetainItem sends content, document_id, timestamp, context, metadata and tags. It sends no entities.
findings.opportunity: Pass the filer's canonical name, and the universe companies a section names, as entities. Then 'Lumentum', 'Lumentum Holdings Inc.' and 'LITE' anchor to one entity node, which is the path graph expansion and multi-hop pointers follow.

findings.topic: model split: routing changes only extraction
findings.statement: Metadata routing (0.10.0) picks only the member that extracts an item. Recall, reflect, consolidation, mental-model refresh and dry-run extraction all stay on the primary LLM. Routing is applied per item, nothing about it is stored, and reprocess replays the original metadata. Separate CONSOLIDATION_LLM_* and per-operation chains exist, and MENTAL_MODEL_REFRESH inherits the reflect chain. The docs say nothing on whether mixing an extraction model with a different consolidation model is a problem.
findings.quote: It is not a data boundary: the facts extracted from a routed document are stored in the same bank as everything else, and recall, reflect, consolidation, mental-model refresh and dry-run extraction all continue to use the primary LLM.
findings.atlas_today: ATLAS_RETAIN_EXTRACTOR=minimax routes Atlas's retains to MiniMax. Consolidation, reflect and mental-model refresh run on the shared primary, openai-codex, which Atlas does not count against any budget.
findings.opportunity: Accept that consolidation quality and quota stay on Codex. If observation quality matters, the owner could set a CONSOLIDATION_* chain, but that is server-wide.

findings.topic: Codex primary: reflect breaks when the token is shared
findings.statement: When a long-running Hindsight shares ~/.codex/auth.json with another Codex process, a rotated single-use refresh token makes /reflect fail while recall and /health keep working. The fix is a dedicated CODEX_HOME; 0.10.0 added a separate credential directory for each Codex member.
findings.quote: Recall and `/health` keep working (the database and API are fine), but
findings.atlas_today: The shared server's primary is Codex, whose quota is shared with hermes, the Codex CLI and LiteLLM's ChatGPT alias (docs/decisions.md). Atlas's reflect, mental-model refresh and the consolidation behind its observations all depend on that primary.
findings.opportunity: Treat a reflect failure while recall succeeds as a credential problem rather than an outage, and confirm with the owner that the Hindsight pod has its own CODEX_HOME.

findings.statement: A model that isn't in the tested list must support at least 65,000 output tokens. RETAIN_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS defaults to 64000 and must exceed RETAIN_CHUNK_SIZE (3000). MiniMax-M3 is the `minimax` provider's default model, but it is not in the 'Tested Models' table, and its output ceiling is not documented.
findings.quote: Other LLM models not listed above may work with Hindsight, but they must support **at least 65,000 output tokens** to ensure reliable fact extraction.
findings.atlas_today: Atlas extracts with MiniMax-M3 with thinking disabled. The bake-off found 16 of 17 expected facts, using two small documents.
findings.opportunity: Check MiniMax-M3's real output limit through LiteLLM. If it is lower, the server's RETAIN_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS must be lowered, or long chunks could be truncated.

findings.statement: Indexed chain members take their own EXTRA_BODY. No fallback to the global value is listed (unlike _REASONING_EFFORT, which falls back). The bake-off found that MiniMax-M3's thinking is disabled only through EXTRA_BODY when it sits behind provider=openai.
findings.quote: | `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_<n>_EXTRA_BODY` / `_DEFAULT_HEADERS` | Per-member JSON overrides. | - |
findings.atlas_today: unknown: the shared server's member-1 settings live in home-ops PR #7180, which is not in this repo.
findings.opportunity: Confirm with the owner that HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_1_EXTRA_BODY disables MiniMax thinking. Otherwise routed extraction runs with thinking on, which was never tested and is slower.

findings.topic: observation dedup and proof count are not independence
findings.statement: Since 0.8.0, consolidation merges near-duplicate observations semantically, and this is on by default. Each observation references its source memories and carries a proof count. So a statement repeated across many filings by the same company becomes one observation with a high proof count.
findings.quote: **Evidence tracking**: Each observation references the source memories (with exact quotes) that support it, plus a proof count
findings.atlas_today: Atlas resolves observations through source_memory_ids and judges independence by Evidence Family, not by Hindsight.
findings.opportunity: Never read an observation's proof count or number of sources as corroboration. Repeated 10-K/10-Q boilerplate inflates it.

findings.topic: reflect answers from mental models first
findings.statement: Reflect checks mental models before observations and raw facts. Since 0.8.0 it skips its extra LLM call when a fresh mental model can answer directly. ReflectRequest supports exclude_mental_models and exclude_mental_model_ids.
findings.quote: Reflect checks mental models first, so a fresh one can answer without descending into observations and raw facts.
findings.atlas_today: The reflect body is query, tags, tags_match, include.facts and an optional response_schema. It never excludes the Theme status or Bottlenecks models.
findings.opportunity: Pass exclude_mental_models for research reflects whose citations must resolve to Source Version sections. Whether a tag-scoped reflect uses the untagged models is not documented.

findings.statement: 0.8.4 added prefer_observations (drops raw facts an observation in the results supersedes and backfills the freed slots), per-stage scores, min_scores and recency decay. 0.9.2 added an explicit temporal_window. Recency is anchored on query_timestamp. max_tokens defaults to 4096.
findings.quote: Recall supports configurable recency decay (linear, exponential, or none) to tune ranking toward recent memory.
