findings.atlas_today: The recall body is query, budget (default 'mid'), tags and tags_match. It sends no query_timestamp, prefer_observations, max_tokens or scores, and pointer weight is 1/rank.
findings.opportunity: Send query_timestamp equal to the investigation's as_of, so recency is scored from the research date. Try prefer_observations, so each pointer recall reaches more distinct sections. Consider a higher max_tokens or budget for pointer recalls.

findings.statement: Since 0.10.0, reflect no longer gives a value for a period the memories don't cover. It says the data isn't recorded instead of extrapolating from neighbouring periods. Also since 0.10.0, reflect fails when its retrieval tools fail, and since 0.9.2 it fails when it produces no answer.
findings.quote: Reflect no longer states a specific value for a period the memories don't cover — it says the data isn't recorded instead of extrapolating a number from neighbouring periods.
findings.atlas_today: The bank template's 'Never fabricate figures' directive asks for the same thing.
findings.opportunity: none; expect more 'not recorded' answers, and more failed reflect jobs where earlier versions returned partial answers.

findings.topic: metadata goes into the extraction prompt
findings.statement: Item metadata is not a filter. It is included in the fact-extraction prompt as context and returned with every recalled memory.
findings.quote: **Included in the fact extraction prompt**, so the LLM can use it as additional context when extracting facts
findings.atlas_today: The metadata is source_version_id, section_anchor, char_start, char_end, available_at, and extractor when set. These are IDs and offsets the extractor can't use; form, company and period reach it only through context ('<title>: <heading>').
findings.opportunity: Add human-readable keys (company display name, form, fiscal period, filer role) that help the extractor attribute and date facts, while keeping the provenance keys.

findings.topic: entity labels as hard recall filters
findings.statement: An entity-label group with tag: true writes each extracted label as a tag, which then works as a SQL-level filter before ranking. 0.10.0 added multi-valued open-text labels.
findings.quote: This is a SQL-level filter applied before ranking, not a scoring signal — the excluded memories never enter the retrieval pipeline.
findings.atlas_today: Tags are set only by Atlas (company, theme, source, document type, form). The bank template defines no entity labels.
findings.opportunity: Have the extractor label each fact with a supply-chain layer or statement kind (capacity, customer, supply agreement) so pointer recall can be filtered hard by layer. This needs a template change and only applies to facts retained afterwards.

findings.statement: Since 0.8.6, an async retain accepts a client-supplied operation_id. Resubmitting with the same ID returns the original operation and creates no new work.
findings.quote: Retain: async retries are now idempotent via caller-supplied operation_id.
findings.atlas_today: The retain_batch body is only items + async (`"items": [item.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True) for item in items],`), so a lost acknowledgement leads to a second operation.
findings.opportunity: Send a deterministic UUID per (job, attempt-batch) as operation_id, so a timed-out submit doesn't cause a duplicate extraction that spends budget.

findings.statement: Async retain splits large batches into sub-batches and extracts in RETAIN_CHUNK_SIZE pieces (3,000 characters by default), each producing about 17 facts. Larger chunks mean fewer LLM calls but may lose context. The docs disagree on whether the 10,000 split threshold counts tokens or characters.
findings.quote: | `HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_CHUNK_SIZE` | Max characters per chunk for fact extraction. Larger chunks extract fewer LLM calls but may lose context. | `3000` |
findings.atlas_today: Atlas sends whole SEC Item sections as single items. Other text goes in chunks of at most 12,000 chars. Hindsight then re-chunks every item at 3,000 chars.
findings.opportunity: none on Atlas's side. Content-loss bugs with oversized items were fixed in 0.8.3 and 0.10.0, and a section's extraction quality depends on 3,000-char windows, not on Atlas's sectioning.

findings.statement: Vector search takes 10-50 ms on 100K+ facts, and the docs say it has been tested with millions of facts per bank. A recall takes 50-100 ms without a reranker and 200-500 ms with one. The reranker considers up to 300 candidates by default.
findings.quote: - **Typical query time**: 10-50ms for vector search on 100K+ facts
findings.atlas_today: Atlas reranks remotely through LiteLLM's `rerank` model and runs one recall per Scout query.
findings.opportunity: none; at Atlas's scale (filings for 12 companies), bank size won't make recall slow.

findings.statement: 0.10.0 fixed retain chunk-ID collisions between banks, and 0.9.1 fixed document statements being shared across banks.
findings.quote: Retain operations no longer risk chunk ID collisions between banks.
findings.atlas_today: Atlas retains the same srcv: document IDs into the research bank and into throwaway evaluation banks on the same server.
findings.opportunity: none on 0.10.x; this is why evaluation banks on the shared server are safe now.

findings.statement: A pending_consolidation counter that never falls usually means operations claimed by a worker that no longer exists, because HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_ID is unstable. The Helm StatefulSet sets a stable ID.
findings.quote: The root cause is almost always an unstable `HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_ID`.
findings.atlas_today: The local compose sets HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_ID: atlas-hindsight-1. The cluster uses Helm.
findings.opportunity: When observations stop appearing, check /banks/{id}/stats pending_consolidation before blaming the LLM.

findings.statement: The default embedder and reranker are English-only, and native BM25 uses PostgreSQL's English dictionary, which gives poor non-English results and no CJK tokenization.
findings.quote: The default `native` backend uses PostgreSQL's English dictionary
findings.atlas_today: Atlas retains only English. Embeddings are qwen3-embedding-0.6b and reranking is LiteLLM `rerank`.
findings.opportunity: Only relevant if AMF (French) or HKEX (Chinese) documents are ever retained. That would need pgroonga and a multilingual reranker.

not_covered: I did not read the changelog past the 0.8.0 entry. The vendored changelog has no 0.10.1 or 0.10.2 entry, so changes after 0.10.0 are not covered.
configuration.md: I read only the retain table, the multi-LLM chain and metadata-routing rows, and the per-operation LLM rows. Its other sections are the config reader's.
The external Model Leaderboard (benchmarks.hindsight.vectorize.io) is not vendored and was not read.

Not settled from the docs: whether recency decay is on by default; whether a tag-scoped reflect uses untagged mental models; how many facts recall's default max_tokens=4096 returns; whether chain members inherit the global EXTRA_BODY; MiniMax-M3's output-token ceiling; how many hops graph expansion goes.
I did not read the full models.md sections for providers Atlas doesn't use (Nous, Claude Code, Cursor, SuperGrok, Azure, Vertex), or the reranker configuration examples.
I did not check the spike recordings for whether 0.10.1 responses include per-stage scores or attachments.
contradictions: The vendored changelog's newest entry is 0.10.0, with no 0.10.1 entry. compose.yaml and the feature matrix pin 0.10.1-slim, while ticket 18 and docs/decisions.md call the cluster 'Hindsight 0.10.2 (the cluster's version)'.

FAQ: tag filtering returns 'Only memories tagged with a matching value', but the feature matrix observed that tags_match=any also returns untagged memories (the matrix wins). Atlas uses only any_strict/all_strict, so it is unaffected.

performance.md says async auto-split happens at '>10,000 tokens' and 'counts real tokens, not characters', but configuration.md defines HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_BATCH_TOKENS as 'Max characters per sub-batch' (default 10000).
performance.md says retain 'Doesn't Need a Smart Model' (recommends gpt-oss-20b). Atlas's bake-off found real model differences: M2.7 paraphrased every quote and found fewer facts than M3.

docs/decisions.md's early entry chose 'MiniMax-M3 ... for both extraction and reflect'. The later metadata-routing decision and configuration.md show that on the shared server reflect, consolidation and mental-model refresh run on the Codex primary, so in production only extraction uses MiniMax.

developer/index.md says mission, directives and disposition 'only affect the reflect operation', while configuration.md has a retain_mission that steers extraction. The bank template sets retain_mission. 'Mission' in index.md means reflect_mission.

result.summary:
Atlas retains each Source Version as one async batch. Each section becomes its own document: id `srcv:<uuid>:<anchor>`, content the exact parsed slice (10-K/10-Q/8-K Items are unbounded, other text is cut into chunks of at most 12k chars), timestamp = available_at, context `<company form filed date>: <heading>`, five string metadata keys, and tags for company, theme, source, doctype and form. It never sends entities, observation_scopes, strategy, update_mode or a client operation_id.

Recall sends only query, budget=mid and tags with any_strict. Investigations scope by theme only. Atlas drops scores, entities, chunks and source_facts, keeps every result, and makes one GET per recalled observation to find its sources. Reflect sends query, tags, include.facts and an optional schema. It sends no budget, so the server default `low` applies, and no max_tokens.

Biggest risk (my reading of the docs, not observed): the default observation scope is the full tag set matched all_strict. Because Atlas's tags include form/source/doctype/company, observations would form only within one company and one form, never across companies.

Failures: there is one operation per version. Any non-quota/outage error, including a missing message, a timeout or a 500, marks every section of that version `failed` without checking documents. `failed` is never retried automatically, and the metric counts current row states.

findings.statement: By default each retained memory's observations are consolidated in one scope made of all its tags, and existing observations are matched all_strict, so only observations whose tag set equals the scope are updated. Atlas sends no observation_scopes, so this default applies to every item.
findings.quote: During consolidation, Hindsight uses `all_strict` matching to find existing observations to update — only observations whose tags exactly match the current scope are considered.
findings.atlas_today: RetainItem has no observation_scopes field (extra="forbid"), so the default `combined` scope applies.
findings.opportunity: Send observation_scopes, e.g. [["theme:photonics"],["company:<uuid>"]] or "shared", so observations consolidate across forms and across companies. Check GET .../observations/scopes on production first.

findings.statement: Every retain item carries company, all themes of the company, source:<provider>, doctype:<source_type> and form:<form_type>. Under the combined default this probably splits observations by company × form × source: a company's 10-K facts apart from its 10-Q, 8-K and transcript facts, and nothing across companies. This is inferred from the docs, not observed.
findings.quote: tags.append(f"form:{version.form_type}")
findings.atlas_today: Tags are used only to scope recall and reflect (company/theme any_strict). source, doctype and form are never queried by Atlas's research reads.
findings.opportunity: Keep the provenance tags for filtering, but set observation_scopes so they are not a consolidation boundary.

findings.statement: All submitted sections of a Source Version go in one operation. When it ends non-completed with a non-transient error class, every pending section of that operation is set failed. No document is checked on this path, so sections a successful sub-batch extracted are still marked failed.
findings.quote: "retain_state = 'failed', error = :error",
findings.atlas_today: The poll job marks every pending row of the operation failed with the operation's error. child_operations are used only to classify the error.
findings.opportunity: Decide each section's outcome per document (GET /documents/{id}) even on a failed operation, or submit smaller batches, so one bad chunk does not fail a whole 10-K.

findings.statement: Only quota and outage texts are transient. Anything else, including a failure with no message, an LLM timeout ("timeout" / "timed out" is not matched) or a relayed 500, is permanent and final.
findings.quote: r"\b50[234]\b|service[ _-]?unavailable|bad gateway|gateway[ _-]?time-?out"
findings.atlas_today: Permanent failures are final: failed sections are not retried automatically. An owner-run retry_failed resets them to pending.
findings.opportunity: Classify extraction timeouts and context-length errors explicitly, and record the error text distribution before tuning.

findings.statement: An SEC primary document's Item is one Hindsight document of unbounded length, and Hindsight chunks it internally. Other text is cut into chunks of at most 12,000 characters.
findings.quote: Items aren't split further: a 140k-character Risk Factors section is one Hindsight document, and Hindsight chunks it internally.
findings.atlas_today: Large Items such as Risk Factors and MD&A go to Hindsight as single items in one batch per version.
findings.opportunity: Bound Item sections (sub-sections) to reduce per-item extraction failures and give finer pointer and provenance granularity.

findings.statement: After a completed operation, a section's fact count is GET /documents/{id}.memory_unit_count. 0 triggers one reprocess (re-retain under the same ID), then zero_fact. A 404 is failed. result_metadata such as extraction_errors_count is stored but never read.
findings.quote: counts[row["id"]] = self._gateway.get_document(document).memory_unit_count
findings.atlas_today: Zero facts lead to one reprocess, then the zero_fact state. Memory IDs are listed via memories/list?document_id and stored on the row.
findings.opportunity: Use extraction_errors_count to tell 'nothing material' from 'extraction failed'.

findings.statement: content is the exact slice of the recorded parsed text, timestamp is the version's available_at (filing/dissemination time, not the reporting period), context is '<title>: <heading or anchor>', and metadata holds source_version_id, section_anchor, char_start, char_end and available_at as strings (plus extractor when routed).
findings.quote: context=f"{version.title}: {heading or anchor}",
findings.atlas_today: For SEC the title is '<company> <form> filed <date>[, <exhibit type>]'. A chunk's context ends 'chunk-003', the cover's 'cover'. No fiscal period is in the context.
findings.opportunity: Add the fiscal period/report date to the context and consider passing entities (company display names) so extraction and entity resolution anchor on the universe.

findings.topic: fields Atlas never sends on retain
findings.statement: RetainItem allows only content, document_id, timestamp, context, metadata and tags. Entities, resolve_entities, observation_scopes, strategy and update_mode cannot be sent. The request has async: true and no client operation_id.
findings.quote: """One document of a retain batch (for Atlas: one section of a Source Version)."""
findings.atlas_today: Only the six modelled fields are sent. A crash between submit and record leads to a resubmission without an idempotency key.
findings.opportunity: Add entities (universe company names), observation_scopes and a client operation_id (idempotent retries).

findings.statement: Recall sends only query, budget (default mid) and tags plus tags_match (any_strict). It sends no types, max_tokens (server default 4096), include (chunks or source_facts), prefer_observations, query_timestamp, temporal_window or min_scores.
findings.quote: body: dict[str, JsonValue] = {"query": query, "budget": budget, **_scope_fields(scope)}
findings.atlas_today: API recall, Scout and Skeptic pointers, and replays all use this. Investigations scope by theme tag only.
findings.opportunity: Pass types/prefer_observations to control fact vs observation mix, include.source_facts to skip per-observation GETs, query_timestamp = as_of for recency anchoring, and max_tokens to control result count.

findings.statement: RecallResult keeps only 'results'. trace, entities, chunks and source_facts are dropped. Per memory, scores, entities and attachments are not modelled, and source_fact_ids (the recall's name for an observation's sources) is not read, so each recalled observation costs a GET /memories/{id}.
findings.quote: # A recall result carries no source IDs; the memory lookup does.
findings.atlas_today: Relevance scores and entities are discarded. Rank is the only relevance signal kept (in reading pointers).
findings.opportunity: Keep scores.final/reranker for pointer weighting and a cut-off, and use entities to name the companies a memory involves.

findings.statement: A fact resolves only when its document_id starts 'srcv:', a memory_document row in this bank has that ID, and the fact's metadata.source_version_id (and section_anchor if present) agree. An observation resolves through source_memory_ids, up to 3 hops, worst hop wins. Content with no memory ID (reflect chunk content) is unverified, and a 404 is broken.
findings.quote: content drawn from a raw chunk, with no memory identity to follow
findings.atlas_today: Only resolved memories become Evidence or reading pointers. Unverified and broken memories are counted and dropped from pointers.
findings.opportunity: none

findings.statement: A pointer's rank is the memory's position in the recall's full result list (unresolved memories counted). One pointer is stored per resolved memory per distinct section, dropping sections available after as_of. Scores, entities and dates are not kept.
findings.quote: for rank, memory in enumerate(response.memories, start=1):
findings.atlas_today: Stored: query index/text/kind, rank, memory id/type/text, section and offsets, company, available_at.
findings.opportunity: Store the recall score so rank cut-offs and weights can use it.

findings.statement: The Scout's (and the Skeptic's) pointer recalls are scoped to the investigation's theme tag only, any_strict, with the default budget mid.
findings.quote: scope = ResearchScope(theme_ids=[theme_id])
findings.atlas_today: Up to 11 Scout recalls and 36 Skeptic recalls per task. No LLM call, no budget counted.
findings.opportunity: Use budget high for the few Scout recalls, or tag_groups to combine theme and company for the Skeptic's company-specific queries.

findings.statement: Companies are ranked by the sum of 1/rank over the Scout pointers naming them. There is no score cut-off and no normalisation by how much of a company is retained.
findings.quote: (slug, sum((Fraction(1, rank) for rank in each), Fraction(0)), min(each), len(each))
findings.atlas_today: Researched non-seed companies get Investigators in this order while max_companies (6) has room.
findings.opportunity: Weight by recall score rather than rank alone.

findings.statement: Within the pointed section, a pointer selects the window whose words overlap most with the memory's text. That text is Hindsight's rewritten fact, including its '| When: … | Involving: …' suffix.
findings.quote: best = _best_window(query_terms(pointer.memory_text), words[index], within)
findings.atlas_today: The memory text is used only to find a window and is never sent to a role.
findings.opportunity: Use the fact's chunk_id/chunk text (include.chunks) to locate the exact span instead of term overlap.

findings.statement: Reflect sends query, tags plus any_strict, include.facts and an optional response_schema. It sends no budget, so the server default 'low' applies per the pinned OpenAPI, and no max_tokens, fact_types or exclude_mental_models.
findings.quote: body: dict[str, Any] = {"query": query, **_scope_fields(scope)}
findings.atlas_today: Used by POST /memory/reflect (a job) and replays. Investigations do not reflect. Stored: text, structured output, raw and resolved citations, tokens.
findings.opportunity: Pass budget mid/high for research questions and fact_types to keep reflect on resolvable facts and observations.

findings.statement: Both template mental models have max_tokens 2048 and no tags, refresh only on a 06:00 cron with a 12 h floor (never after consolidation), and the daily Atlas job skips them when they are not stale.
findings.quote: Both have `max_tokens` 2048, no tags (the bank holds only Atlas-retained, tagged material)
findings.atlas_today: Stored per refresh: content, sha256, raw based_on memories, refreshed_at, operation result_metadata. Citations are resolved on read.
findings.opportunity: none

findings.topic: linked versions keep no own tags
findings.statement: A byte-identical Source Version is linked to the retained twin and not retained, so its own company or theme tags never reach memory.
findings.quote: The linked copy's own tags (for example a different company) are not in memory; the retained twin's are.
findings.atlas_today: Recall scoped to the linked copy's company cannot find it.
findings.opportunity: none

findings.statement: atlas_retained_sections_total counts memory_document rows by their current retain_state, so it is a snapshot of rows, and failed rows stay failed until retry_failed is run.
findings.quote: _FINAL_SECTION_STATES = ("completed", "zero_fact", "failed", "linked")
findings.atlas_today: Rows failed under older rules (e.g. 'no healthy deployments' was permanent before ticket 11) remain counted as failed.
findings.opportunity: Query memory_document.error grouped by text to see which failure dominates.

contradictions: The pinned .agents/skills/hindsight-docs/references/openapi.json reports info.version "0.10.0", while the skill and feature matrix say v0.10.1.

docs/decisions.md (retention) says 'Failed sections are not retried automatically' and that a failed/cancelled/not_found operation marks sections failed. The later queue-pause entry and ticket 11 changed this for quota/outage errors (sections stay pending and are resubmitted), and ticket 11 reclassified 'no healthy deployments' from permanent to unavailable. Rows failed before the change remain failed.

decisions ('Memory as the reading index', 'Multi-hop Investigators') expects theme-scoped recall to surface cross-company knowledge. Under the documented default observation scope (all tags combined, all_strict) and Atlas's per-item tags, observations would never span companies or forms, so only raw facts can cross companies (my inference, not observed).

The feature matrix says reflect based_on memories lack document_id. models.py CitedMemory matches this, so there is no contradiction there. The recall recording shows 'source_fact_ids', while Atlas's Memory model reads 'source_memory_ids' (present only on GET /memories/{id}). This is handled by an extra lookup, not a bug.
not_covered: Whether one failed chunk or sub-batch fails the whole Hindsight retain operation, and whether documents of successful sub-batches persist (not in my slice's docs).

How the job queue treats a poll_operation job that failed after its 5 attempts: sections would stay pending with an operation_id and retain() does not resubmit them. Unverified whether _enqueue_polls can re-create the job under the same key.
Production numbers and error texts: no network call was made, so the failed-vs-completed explanation is code paths only.
atlas.research.quotes, atlas.research.search, the investigation task runner beyond the recall call sites, and how the Scout uses the Bottlenecks mental-model content.

Hindsight concept pages (retain, recall, retrieval, observations, best-practices) beyond the specific lines quoted. The observation-scope reading should be confirmed by the lead's observations slice or GET .../observations/scopes.

checked.statement: Qwen3-Embedding models expect an instruction in front of each search query. Hindsight adds it automatically only with the `local` provider. For plain-text providers (openai, tei, litellm) the operator must set HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_PREFIX (and PASSAGE_PREFIX if needed). This is a static server setting. An instruction on the search side only needs no re-indexing.
checked.quote: The default `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` ships none, so nothing changes for existing deployments; `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-*` ships one for searches only, which is what makes those models retrieve accurately.
checked.atlas_today: compose.yaml (which states it mirrors the cluster) runs qwen3-embedding-0.6b through HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=openai via LiteLLM and sets no QUERY_PREFIX, so recall queries and Scout pointer queries are embedded without the instruction. I did not verify the cluster env in home-ops.
checked.opportunity: Set HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_QUERY_PREFIX to Qwen3's query instruction on the server, with no re-index. Then compare recall and pointer quality before and after on the pilot question set.

checked.topic: Embeddings: similarity gates calibrated for another model
checked.statement: Five cosine gates were calibrated for bge-small-en-v1.5 and the docs say to recalibrate all of them after a model change: semantic retrieval 0.3, graph seed 0.3, temporal 0.1, semantic links at retain 0.7, observation dedup 0.97. All are server env. The semantic-link threshold acts at retain time and is not applied retroactively.
checked.quote: configured independently. Their defaults preserve the behavior calibrated for `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`.
checked.atlas_today: Atlas uses qwen3-embedding-0.6b at 1024 dims with every gate at its default (none set in compose.yaml).
checked.opportunity: Measure the cosine distributions of qwen3 on Atlas's facts and recalibrate the gates, above all SEMANTIC_LINK_MIN_SIMILARITY, which sets graph density for every future retain. Do it before the bulk universe backfill, because it is not retroactive.

checked.topic: Consolidation: observations_mission replaces the built-in rules
checked.statement: Setting observations_mission (per bank or server) replaces Hindsight's default definition of an observation entirely. The default definition is durable, specific beliefs grounded in source memories, ephemeral state filtered out, and contradictions tracked with temporal markers rather than overwritten. Only the bank's mission text then guides what consolidation creates or updates.
checked.quote: Set `HINDSIGHT_API_OBSERVATIONS_MISSION` to replace this definition entirely.
checked.atlas_today: configs/hindsight/bank-template.json sets a one-sentence observations_mission ("Consolidate independently grounded industry developments while recording contradictions, conditionality and changed circumstances..."), so the default rules are gone.
checked.opportunity: Rewrite the mission so it carries what Atlas needs from the defaults: per-company specificity, temporal markers on changed facts (as of which filing or period), keeping figures with unit and period, and supplier/customer relationships. Observations are what reflect cites and what Atlas resolves through source_memory_ids.

checked.topic: Entity resolution: fuzzy matching, 7-day temporal signal
checked.statement: An extracted name is matched against existing entities in two stages. Stage 1: trigram ≥ 0.15, at most 200 candidates. Stage 2: a candidate is reused if its score clears 0.6, from name similarity (up to 0.5), co-occurring entities (up to 0.3) and temporal proximity (up to 0.2, decaying to zero at 7 days from the candidate's last_seen). It must also reach a trigram floor of 0.3 and agree word by word. Label entities resolve by exact match only. All thresholds are server env.
checked.quote: How close the fact's date is to the candidate's `last_seen`, decaying linearly to zero at 7 days
checked.atlas_today: Atlas relies on free-form fuzzy resolution. Its filings are dated by available_at, months apart, so the temporal signal contributes nothing. Name variants such as 'Coherent Corp.', 'Coherent' and 'II-VI' must merge on name and co-occurrence alone, or stay separate entities.
checked.opportunity: Give Hindsight Atlas's resolved identities so graph expansion (entity co-occurrence) follows real companies across filings: user-provided item entities with resolve_entities false, or per-bank entity_labels. See the next finding.

checked.statement: entity_labels (a controlled vocabulary) and entities_allow_free_form (default true) are set per bank, not by env, and can also be overridden per retain strategy. Both appear in the bank-template schema. Items can carry their own entities (RetainContent.entities). In chunks mode these are the only entity data.
checked.quote: are configured per bank via the [bank config API](api/memory-banks.md#retain-configuration), not as global environment variables
checked.atlas_today: Resolved config shows entity_labels null and entities_allow_free_form true. RetainItem in backend/atlas/hindsight/models.py has no entities field.
checked.opportunity: Add the universe and counterparty companies (canonical names) to each section's retain item as entities, or as a label vocabulary in the template. Then entity links in the graph and co-occurrence match Atlas's identity layer, which multi-hop supply-chain recall depends on. Check the field format in api/retain.md first.

checked.statement: A bank can define named retain_strategies, each a set of hierarchical overrides (extraction mode, chunk size, structured chunk size, entity_labels, free-form, retain_mission, ...). A retain call picks one with `strategy`; otherwise retain_default_strategy applies. The docs show the strategy chosen per call, not per item.
checked.quote: Named strategies let you ingest different content types into the same bank using different extraction settings. A strategy is a set of hierarchical field overrides applied on top of the resolved bank config.
checked.atlas_today: No strategies are defined. The gateway posts {items, async: true} with no strategy, so 10-K Items, 8-K exhibits and TradingView transcripts all get one mission and the concise mode.
checked.opportunity: Define strategies per document type in the bank template. For example, a transcript mission for management statements on capacity, customers and lead times, verbose mode for exhibits and press releases, and the filings mission for 10-K/10-Q Items. Pass `strategy` per batch (Atlas batches per Source Version already). Compare strategies first with the dry-run extract endpoint.

checked.statement: retain_extraction_mode is one of concise (the default), verbose, verbatim, chunks or custom. It can be set on the server, per bank or per strategy. Verbose gives richer facts that keep context and relationships, at more tokens. Verbatim stores each chunk exactly as one memory and still runs the LLM for entities, time and place. Chunks makes no LLM call. Custom replaces the selectivity rules but keeps output format, temporal handling and coreference.
checked.quote: Each chunk is stored as a single memory unit with its original text preserved exactly — no summarization or rewriting.
checked.atlas_today: concise (resolved config recording). Atlas never quotes memory text: the memories only choose sections.
checked.opportunity: Atlas uses memories only as pointers to sections, so verbose (relationship qualifiers kept) or verbatim (the chunk text itself indexed, entities still extracted) could make better pointers. Try them per strategy on recorded filings with dry-run extract before changing the bank.

checked.statement: By default a retain whose fact extraction hit errors is still marked completed, and the facts it lost are dropped silently. With HINDSIGHT_API_FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS=true such a retain is marked failed, with the error count. It is a static server setting.
checked.quote: When `true`, a retain operation that accumulated any fact-extraction errors is marked `failed` (with an error message including the count) instead of `completed`, so silently-dropped facts surface as a hard failure.
checked.atlas_today: Not set (default false). Atlas's poll_operation treats completed as retained, so a long Item with a failed chunk would look fully retained.
checked.opportunity: Set it to true on the server. Atlas's retain/poll path already retries failed operations, so lost chunks become retries instead of gaps in the index.

checked.statement: Extraction runs one LLM call per chunk of at most retain_chunk_size characters (default 3000; server, bank or strategy). Each chunk yields roughly 17 facts. Chunk boundaries and token counts use HINDSIGHT_API_TOKENIZER_ENCODING (o200k_base). This page documents no overlap setting and no boundary rule.
checked.quote: Max characters per chunk for fact extraction. Larger chunks extract fewer LLM calls but may lose context.
checked.atlas_today: Default 3000. Atlas sections are whole SEC Items (often tens of thousands of characters) or chunks of up to MAX_CHUNK_CHARS = 12_000, so Hindsight re-splits each one. Each 3000-character piece is extracted with only the item's `context` ('title: heading') as document-level framing.
checked.opportunity: Tune retain_chunk_size per strategy (e.g. larger for transcripts, so a Q&A answer stays with its question). Check in retain.md whether `context` reaches every chunk's prompt. Atlas's char offsets in metadata already let it locate a fact's section.

checked.statement: Causal links between facts are extracted by default (server-only setting). Semantic links are created at retain for pairs at or above cosine 0.7, which sets graph density and is not retroactive. The default graph retriever, link_expansion, expands from semantic seeds through entity co-occurrence, semantic kNN and causal links.
checked.quote: Fast graph expansion from semantic seeds via entity co-occurrence, semantic kNN, and causal links.
checked.atlas_today: Defaults: causal links on, semantic link threshold 0.7 (calibrated for another embedding model).
checked.opportunity: Keep causal links on. Multi-hop recall rides on entity, semantic and causal links, so entity identity and semantic-link calibration are what to work on (findings above).

checked.topic: Metadata routing: only extraction moves, consolidation stays on the primary
checked.statement: Metadata routing chooses the member that extracts each item. The choice is not stored, and reprocessing replays the original metadata. Recall, reflect, consolidation, mental-model refresh and dry-run extraction stay on the primary LLM. Each operation can have its own chain, including CONSOLIDATION.
checked.quote: Each operation can define its own members + strategy with the `RETAIN` / `REFLECT` / `CONSOLIDATION` / `MENTAL_MODEL_REFRESH` prefix
checked.atlas_today: ATLAS_RETAIN_EXTRACTOR=minimax adds extractor: minimax to item metadata. docs/decisions.md already notes that consolidation of those facts still spends the ChatGPT (primary) quota, uncounted by Atlas.
checked.opportunity: Configure a HINDSIGHT_API_CONSOLIDATION_LLM_* chain on MiniMax (or count consolidation against codex). Note that dry-run extract tests the primary, not the routed member.

checked.statement: Consolidation runs automatically after retain, delete and update (enable_auto_consolidation, per bank). It sends 8 facts per LLM call (per bank) and handles at most 100 memories per round before re-queuing (per bank). Mental-model refreshes run only on the final round. Source facts in the prompt are capped at 4096 tokens in total and 256 per observation (per bank). Near-duplicate observations at cosine ≥ 0.97 go to a merge-or-keep LLM call (server).
checked.quote: When the limit is reached, the job yields its worker slot and re-queues itself so other banks get fair scheduling. Mental model refreshes only run on the final round.
checked.atlas_today: All defaults. Mental models refresh on a daily cron with refresh_after_consolidation false, so the final-round coupling does not apply to them.
checked.opportunity: During a bulk backfill, consider enable_auto_consolidation false, then an explicit consolidate (as replay banks already do), so consolidation sees whole filings rather than partial ones. Raise the per-observation source-fact cap if observations about one company draw on many filings.

checked.statement: max_observations_per_scope (default -1, unlimited; per bank) caps observations per tag scope. At the cap, consolidation only updates or deletes. Untagged observations are exempt. Scopes can be per_tag, all_combinations or an explicit list (observation_scopes), but this page only names them.
checked.quote: Applies per tag scope (e.g., per-tag when using `per_tag` observation scopes).
checked.atlas_today: Unlimited. Documents carry observation_scopes null (upsert/09-get-document recording), so the server's default scoping of company/theme tags applies, which this page does not document.
checked.opportunity: Find out in retain.md or observations.md how Atlas's company:/theme: tags group consolidation. Per-company observation scopes would keep observations company-grounded.

checked.statement: retain_mission is added to the extraction prompt next to the built-in rules and narrows focus without replacing them; it is ignored in chunks mode. Custom mode with retain_custom_instructions replaces the selectivity rules but keeps output format, temporal handling and coreference resolution.
checked.quote: The mission is injected into the extraction prompt alongside the built-in rules — it narrows focus without replacing the underlying logic.
checked.atlas_today: retain_mission is set (economically material facts: capacity, supply agreements, customer dependencies, ...). No custom instructions.
checked.opportunity: Keep the mission approach. Add naming the counterparty company in supplier/customer facts, and naming the filer rather than 'we', so that entity links form.

checked.statement: Extracted facts carry when/where/who/why. With HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_OPTIONAL_FACT_DIMENSIONS false (the default, server-only), the model must fill them. Under a strict schema it may then write a date the text gave for something else.
checked.quote: the nearest plausible one is a date the text stated about something else
checked.atlas_today: Default. Atlas sends timestamp = available_at, recorded as retain_params.event_date. LLM_STRICT_SCHEMA is not set.
checked.opportunity: Mostly none. If wrong dates show up on filing facts (filings state many dates), try optional dimensions, and LLM_SUPPORTS_STRING_PATTERN if the backend accepts `pattern`.

checked.topic: Dry-run extraction for testing intake settings
checked.statement: HINDSIGHT_API_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_EXTRACT (default true) exposes POST /banks/{bank_id}/memories/dry-run-extract. It runs extraction with a real LLM call and stores nothing.
checked.quote: Runs extraction only — makes a real LLM call but stores nothing.
checked.atlas_today: Not used.
checked.opportunity: A cheap harness for comparing modes, missions, strategies and chunk sizes on recorded filing sections and transcripts without polluting the research bank. It uses the primary LLM, not metadata routes.

checked.statement: The five embedding gates (semantic 0.3, graph seed 0.3, temporal 0.1, semantic-link creation 0.7, observation dedup 0.97) are calibrated for BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5. The docs say to recalibrate all five when the embedding model changes. Atlas embeds with qwen3-embedding-0.6b, so every gate that admits candidates to recall, builds the semantic graph or dedups observations is uncalibrated for Atlas's corpus.
checked.quote: Their defaults preserve the behavior calibrated for `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`.
checked.atlas_today: Uses qwen3-embedding-0.6b (compose.yaml: `HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_OPENAI_MODEL: qwen3-embedding-0.6b`, the same as the cluster per its comment) with every threshold at its default. No calibration has been done.
checked.opportunity: Measure read-only how qwen3 cosine similarities are distributed on Atlas's own facts and queries (recall traces), then propose threshold values to the owner. Raising or lowering SEMANTIC_MIN_SIMILARITY and SEMANTIC_LINK_MIN_SIMILARITY changes what the reading index can return and how dense the graph is. The link threshold is not retroactive.

checked.statement: The request budget (low/mid/high, default mid) maps to a thinking_budget used by every retrieval arm. Under the default fixed function it is 100/300/1000 items per arm per fact type, independent of max_tokens. It sets how wide retrieval searches before fusion, not how many results are returned. The mapping is per bank (recall_budget_function, recall_budget_fixed_*, adaptive ratios, min/max are all in BankTemplateConfig). The reranker cap can be overridden per budget level server-side.
checked.quote: Items per retrieval method per fact type when `budget=mid` and function is `fixed`. | `300`
checked.atlas_today: Every recall uses the default `budget="mid"` (gateway.recall signature `budget: Budget = "mid"`; research RecallRequest default mid). Pointer recalls pass no budget, max_tokens or types.
checked.opportunity: Try budget=high on the Scout's theme-wide pointer recalls. They make no LLM call, so they cost nothing against the 40-operation budget. With the reranker cap at 300, wider arms mainly change which candidates survive RRF to be reranked. Compare pointer sets at mid and high on the pilot question.

checked.topic: fusion, reranker cap and strategy boosts
checked.statement: Candidates from the four arms are fused by RRF. Only the top HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_MAX_CANDIDATES (300) are reranked, and RRF pre-filters the rest. There is no per-arm cap by default. RECALL_STRATEGY_BOOSTS (server, empty by default) can favour an arm, e.g. graph:low/medium/high, both before the cap and after reranking.
checked.quote: The boost is applied in two places: before the reranker cap (so favoured candidates survive the `HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_MAX_CANDIDATES` budget) and after reranking (to nudge them up the final order)
checked.atlas_today: No boosts. Server defaults on the shared Hindsight (the cluster's env is not in this repo).
checked.opportunity: For multi-hop supply-chain reading, `graph:low` would keep graph-arm hits (company B reached through an entity that co-occurs in A's facts) from being cut before reranking. Only the owner can set it, and it affects every bank on the shared server.

checked.statement: By default a failing reranker fails the recall. A failover chain ending in `rrf` makes recall fail open and return the fusion order. Members are tried in order on every request, with no circuit breaker. Scores are not comparable across providers.
checked.quote: Ending the chain with `rrf` makes recall **fail open**: results come back in the order
checked.atlas_today: compose.yaml uses `HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_PROVIDER: litellm` with model `rerank` and no fallback member. A LiteLLM rerank outage fails every Scout pointer recall (recorded as pointer_recall_failed) and every /memory/recall.
checked.opportunity: Ask the owner to add `HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_1_PROVIDER=rrf` to the shared server, so a rerank outage degrades ranking quality instead of losing all pointers.

checked.statement: During reranking, a memory's age adds a small freshness adjustment to its final rank. The default is linear decay from today to a floor at 365 days (exponential with a 90-day half-life, or none, are the alternatives). The docs do not say which timestamp counts as the age, how large the adjustment is, or whether query_timestamp replaces 'today'.
checked.quote: `linear` (default) decays in a straight line from full freshness (today) to a floor reached at `HINDSIGHT_API_RECENCY_DECAY_LINEAR_WINDOW_DAYS`.
checked.atlas_today: Not considered. Pointer rank is taken as Hindsight returns it (pointer weight = 1/rank).
checked.opportunity: Facts from recent filings get a slight edge, which is mostly desirable. For replay banks at a past cutoff, 'today' is the real date, so recency may rank replayed facts differently from production at that time. Note this as a replay-comparability caveat rather than act on it.

checked.statement: The default text search is native Postgres (english dictionary). Native ranking has no IDF and matches are OR-joined. Queries over 16 terms are trimmed to the 16 most selective terms (lowest document frequency).
checked.quote: because native ranking has no IDF and re-ranks every match
checked.atlas_today: Scout queries, the round's question and bear-checklist items go to recall as written, and the arm is on.
checked.opportunity: Keep pointer-recall queries short and specific: product, layer and company terms, not long sentences. In a photonics bank, common words like 'optical' score like rare ones under a ranking with no IDF.

checked.statement: The only graph retriever is link_expansion. It expands from semantic seeds (cosine >= GRAPH_SEED_MIN_SIMILARITY 0.3) through entity co-occurrence, semantic kNN links (created at retain at cosine >= 0.7) and causal links, with at most 200 targets per entity and a 10 s timeout. Its quality depends on entity resolution at retain time.
checked.quote: Fast graph expansion from semantic seeds via entity co-occurrence, semantic kNN, and causal links. Target latency under 100ms.
checked.atlas_today: The graph arm is on. The template sets no entity_labels. Theme-wide any_strict scoping lets the graph cross companies inside the theme.
checked.opportunity: Multi-hop only works when name variants of a company (legal name, short name, ticker) resolve to one entity. Consider per-bank entity_labels or passing entities at retain for universe companies, and check entity merges in the research bank.

checked.statement: The temporal arm runs on a date constraint parsed from the query text (dateparser; auto-detecting languages is costly) with a 0.1 similarity floor. It adds candidates and filters nothing out. The feature matrix observed that a temporal window is not a hard filter.
checked.quote: a 2024 window still returned 7 of 14 results dated 2026, some ranked first
checked.atlas_today: Atlas applies its own as-of cutoff to pointers (none for a version available after as_of) and never relies on Hindsight's temporal filtering.
checked.opportunity: Keep the Atlas-side cutoff. Leave query dates like 'FY2026' in the query text when the question is period-bound, since that is what activates the arm.

checked.statement: API recall queries longer than 500 tokens are rejected with HTTP 400. Internal recalls (reflect, consolidation, MCP) are truncated instead.
checked.quote: API requests exceeding this limit are rejected with HTTP 400
checked.atlas_today: Scout queries are short. A long investigation question passed straight to recall could hit the limit.
checked.opportunity: Guard or trim question-length recall queries on Atlas's side so a long question does not turn into a failed pointer recall.

checked.topic: reflect internal recall: chunks and fact budget
checked.statement: Reflect's recall tool (also used by mental-model refresh) returns raw chunk text by default (RECALL_INCLUDE_CHUNKS true, 1000 tokens) alongside 2048 tokens of facts. These are set per bank, and per mental model via trigger.include_chunks, recall_max_tokens and recall_chunks_max_tokens. An explicit request from the reflect model wins.
checked.quote: Whether the internal recall returns raw chunk text alongside facts. Set `false` to skip chunks and save prompt budget.
checked.atlas_today: Defaults. The template sets neither recall_include_chunks nor any trigger recall fields. The feature matrix notes that chunk-sourced reflect content cannot be resolved and is labelled unverified.
checked.opportunity: For the mental models and reflect jobs, set include_chunks false and raise recall_max_tokens (e.g. 4096) so syntheses rest on memories Atlas can resolve to Source Version sections. Measure how the share of resolved citations changes.

checked.statement: By default reflect's search_observations tool returns observations without the world facts behind them (REFLECT_SOURCE_FACTS_MAX_TOKENS -1). 0 means unlimited, >0 sets a budget. It is per bank (reflect_source_facts_max_tokens). The search_observations budget defaults to 5000 tokens and can be changed through reflect_default_options.
checked.quote: `-1` disables source facts (default), `0` enables with no limit, `>0` enables with a token budget.
checked.atlas_today: Default (-1). Atlas resolves an observation through source_memory_ids after the fact, but the reflect model reasons from observation text alone.
checked.opportunity: Set reflect_source_facts_max_tokens (e.g. 2000–4000) in the template so reflect and mental models see the grounding facts. This fits the reflect_mission's 'distinguish factual statements'. Consider reflect_search_observations_include_entities false to win back context.

checked.topic: mental models read other mental models
checked.statement: The mental-model trigger's exclude_mental_models defaults to false, so a refresh may call search_mental_models and read other mental models' content. Other trigger fields: fact_types (default all), mode full|delta (default full), keep_trace (default false; the only way to see how a cron refresh reached its result).
checked.quote: If true, exclude all mental models from the reflect loop (skip search_mental_models tool).
checked.atlas_today: configs/hindsight/bank-template.json sets only refresh_after_consolidation false, refresh_cron, min_refresh_interval_seconds and max_tokens. Theme status and Bottlenecks can therefore cite each other's syntheses, which Atlas cannot resolve to a Source Version.
checked.opportunity: Add `exclude_mental_models: true` and `keep_trace: true` to both models' triggers (a template version bump). That keeps each model grounded in memories and records retrieved-vs-used counts for review.

checked.statement: Reflect allows at most 10 tool iterations and 100000 accumulated context tokens before forcing a synthesis, and has a 300 s wall timeout (HTTP 504). The per-call reflect LLM timeout defaults to 30 s. Final synthesis output is uncapped unless REFLECT_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS is set.
checked.quote: | `HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_WALL_TIMEOUT` | Wall-clock timeout in seconds for the entire reflect operation. If exceeded, the request returns HTTP 504. | `300` |
checked.atlas_today: The gateway's `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 300.0` equals the server wall timeout, so a long reflect can race Atlas's client timeout against Hindsight's 504. Compose raises the reflect LLM timeout to 300.
checked.opportunity: Set the client timeout a little above 300 s, so a slow reflect surfaces as Hindsight's 504 (a classified failure) rather than a client timeout. Treat 504 as retryable without spending more budget than needed.

checked.statement: The reflect 'thinking' step samples at temperature 0.9 by default, against 0.1 for retain and 0.0 for consolidation. It is server-level only.
checked.quote: Temperature for the reflect "thinking" step. Number in `[0.0, 2.0]` or `none` to omit. Overrides `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_TEMPERATURE`. | `0.9` |
checked.atlas_today: Default. The daily mental models (mode full) are regenerated from scratch at 0.9, so content can change day to day without new evidence. Atlas skips refreshes that are not stale.
checked.opportunity: Ask the owner for a lower REFLECT (or MENTAL_MODEL_REFRESH extra_body) temperature, or use trigger mode delta so unchanged sections stay byte-for-byte. Either makes mental-model history diffs mean new evidence rather than sampling noise.

checked.topic: per-operation LLM routing and what metadata routing leaves on the primary
checked.statement: Retain, reflect, consolidation and mental-model refresh each have an LLM group and an optional chain (refresh inherits reflect). Metadata routing chooses only the retain extractor. Recall uses no LLM.
checked.quote: recall, reflect, consolidation, mental-model refresh and dry-run extraction all continue to use the primary LLM
checked.atlas_today: Atlas knows this (decisions.md: consolidation of MiniMax-extracted facts still spends the ChatGPT quota, uncounted).
checked.opportunity: The owner could set HINDSIGHT_API_CONSOLIDATION_LLM_* (or a CONSOLIDATION chain) on the shared server to take consolidation off the 40-operations-per-5h primary. MENTAL_MODEL_REFRESH_LLM_* could likewise go to a cheap no-think model. Atlas cannot set either itself.

checked.topic: consolidation batch size (cost lever Atlas owns)
checked.statement: Consolidation sends 8 facts per LLM call by default (per bank). Higher values mean fewer calls but larger prompts. Each new or updated observation at cosine >= 0.97 to an existing one adds a one-by-one merge-or-keep LLM call. Rounds handle at most 100 memories, and mental-model refreshes run only on the final round.
checked.quote: Number of facts sent to the LLM in a single consolidation call. Higher values reduce LLM calls and improve throughput at the cost of larger prompts.
checked.atlas_today: Default 8 (not in the template).
checked.opportunity: Raise consolidation_llm_batch_size in the template (e.g. 16–24) to cut the primary-LLM calls consolidation spends per retained section. Check observation quality on a sample before keeping it.

checked.statement: WORKER_MAX_SLOTS defaults to 10, with 2 reserved for consolidation. Reservations are floors, not caps. Only one consolidation runs per bank at a time, whatever the slots. The poller claims queued work every 500 ms, regardless of the sweep intervals.
checked.quote: Consolidation's bank-serialization constraint (no two consolidation tasks for the same bank concurrently) is preserved regardless of which pool claims the slot.
checked.atlas_today: Local compose uses 4 slots with LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT 2. Everything goes into one research bank, so its consolidation drains serially.
checked.opportunity: After a backfill burst, observations (part of the reading index) lag world facts until the bank's single consolidation chain drains. Pointer recalls taken during a backlog miss new observations. Consider waiting for consolidation to drain (operations API) before a scheduled investigation.

checked.statement: Per bank, the BM25, temporal, graph and reranking stages can each be switched off (semantic always runs). Without reranking, recall returns the RRF order. These are in the recorded BankTemplateConfig.
checked.quote: `false` returns the RRF-fused ordering directly — faster, but less precise.
checked.atlas_today: All on (defaults).
checked.opportunity: None for the research bank. The toggles are useful in evaluation banks to measure each arm's contribution to pointer quality (ablation), without touching production.

checked.statement: GET /memories/list accepts entity_id, an exact reverse lookup over stored entity links. It can be combined with type, tags/tags_match and time_field+start_date/end_date, where the date range filters rather than ranks. Each returned fact carries document_id and metadata. So from one company it lists every fact naming it in any filing, including other companies' filings. Atlas never calls it, and drops the entity IDs that recall already returns.
checked.quote: so you can list an entity's evidence (e.g. its observations, with `type=observation`) without scanning every memory
checked.atlas_today: memories/list is used only with type=observation and document_id (gateway list_observations, document_memories). Entity IDs from recall are discarded.
checked.opportunity: A deterministic, exhaustive, as-of-filterable company-to-company hop. Take the entity_id of a company named in a read filing, list its facts across the bank (tags/time filtered), and turn each fact's metadata.source_version_id/section_anchor into a reading pointer. That reaches suppliers and customers named in other filers' documents, which a theme-scoped top-k recall can miss.

checked.statement: Recall includes entities by default (include.entities default max_tokens 500). The response's entities map gives entity_id and canonical_name for every entity in the results, and the recordings show 17 to 21 entries per recall. Atlas's RecallResult keeps only `results`, and Memory has no entities field.
checked.quote:
class RecallResult(_Result):
    memories: list[Memory] = Field(validation_alias="results")
checked.atlas_today: Drops the per-result entity names and the response-level entity map, which is already paid for in every recall.
checked.opportunity: Keep the entity map so a pointer can carry the entity IDs it mentions. Those IDs feed memories/list?entity_id= and give the ranking of pointed companies an entity-level signal besides the section's company tag.

checked.statement: MemoryItem accepts `entities` (text, optional type), combined with the auto-extracted ones. With resolve_entities=false the names are taken literally. Atlas sends none, and the extractor's resolution split one company into two entities in the recorded recall: 'Aurora Optics' and 'Aurora Optics Inc.', with different entity_ids.
checked.quote: "canonical_name": "Aurora Optics Inc.",
checked.atlas_today: RetainItem has no entities field. Entity identity is left entirely to Hindsight's extractor.
checked.opportunity: Send the filer's canonical name, and Atlas-resolved universe/counterparty names found in the section, as entities with resolve_entities=false. Then each company has one stable entity that entity_id listing, the entity graph and graph-arm recall can follow. Test first with POST /memories/dry-run-extract (no storage).

checked.topic: observation scopes fragmented by Atlas's tags
checked.statement: Per-item observation_scopes defaults to 'combined', a single consolidation pass with all of the item's tags together, and an observation scope is an exact tag set. Atlas tags every item with company, each theme, source, doctype and form, so observations form only among memories with identical tag sets. A company's 10-K facts and its 10-Q or transcript facts fall into different scopes. GET /observations/scopes enumerates the scopes with counts.
checked.quote: 'combined' (default) runs a single pass with all tags together.
checked.atlas_today: No observation_scopes sent. Tags from version_tags include source:, doctype: and form: alongside company: and theme:. POST /consolidate is sent as {} (no scopes).
checked.opportunity: Call GET /observations/scopes to measure fragmentation. Consider explicit scopes such as [["company:<id>"],["theme:<slug>"]] so observations synthesise across a company's filings and across the theme. Confirm the semantics against the observations page (lead's slice) first.

checked.statement: RecallRequest.max_tokens defaults to 4096 and bounds how much the result list holds. Atlas never sends it, so every pointer recall is capped (10 to 14 results in the recordings). budget is always 'mid'. Under the default fixed mapping, low/mid/high mean per-arm retrieval limits of 100/300/1000.
checked.quote: body: dict[str, JsonValue] = {"query": query, "budget": budget, **_scope_fields(scope)}
checked.atlas_today: Sends query, budget (mid by default) and tags only. The Scout's theme recall uses the defaults.
checked.opportunity: Raise max_tokens (and maybe budget=high) for the Scout's pointer recalls. Recall makes no LLM call, so more pointers per query cost latency only, and more of the theme's companies and sections get pointed at.

checked.statement: With include.source_facts, recall returns each observation's source_fact_ids and a source_facts map keyed by fact ID. The map values are full RecallResult objects (document_id, metadata, chunk_id), with source_facts_truncated set when the budget cut it. Atlas instead makes 1 + N GET /memories calls per observation. Not exercised in any recording: without the option, source_fact_ids is null on observations.
checked.quote: Source facts for observation-type results, keyed by fact ID
checked.atlas_today: ProvenanceResolver calls get_memory on the observation, then on each source memory.
checked.opportunity: Request include.source_facts={} on pointer and research recalls and resolve observations from the response. This saves HTTP calls per recall and lets the Scout record observation pointers without extra round trips. Verify against 0.10.1 first, because it is unrecorded.

checked.topic: no date filter in recall; as-of
checked.statement: Recall has no date filter: temporal_window only ranks, and the feature matrix confirmed that a 2024 window still returned 2026 results. query_timestamp anchors recency scoring. memories/list's time_field/start_date/end_date is a real filter. tag_groups support NOT, so tag-based period exclusion is possible.
checked.quote: Used as the query-time anchor for relative temporal expressions and recency scoring.
checked.atlas_today: No query_timestamp. as_of is enforced after recall by dropping pointers to versions available after as_of, so those memories still use up recall slots.
checked.opportunity: Send query_timestamp=as_of for investigations and replays. For hard as-of scoping, either use memories/list with a time window (exhaustive), or tag items with an availability period and exclude later periods with a tag_groups NOT leaf.

checked.topic: scope is a union; tag_groups unused
checked.statement: Atlas builds one tag list of company: and theme: tags with any_strict, which is an OR. Hindsight's tag_groups allow AND/OR/NOT trees of leaves, so scopes like company AND form:10-K or theme AND NOT source:tradingview become possible.
checked.quote: tags = [f"company:{c}" for c in company_ids] + [f"theme:{t}" for t in theme_ids]
checked.atlas_today: A scope of company_ids and theme_ids returns memories of any of them (union). No form/source/doctype scoping, although those tags are written at retain.
checked.opportunity: Use tag_groups with strict leaves (resolve='exact') to target recall at document families, such as periodic reports only or transcripts only, or at a company within a theme. This gives the Skeptic's per-company checklist recalls and the Investigators sharper pointers.

checked.statement: Every recall result carries scores (final, reranker, semantic, keyword). min_scores can set post-ranking floors on reranker/final that every returned result is guaranteed to clear. The schema warns that reranker scores are not calibrated across queries. Atlas keeps only the list order.
checked.quote: post-ranking filters applied to every scored result, so those floors *are* guaranteed by each result returned
checked.atlas_today: Pointer weight is 1/rank (`for rank, memory in enumerate(response.memories, start=1):`). Scores are not parsed.
checked.opportunity: Store scores.final/reranker on each reading pointer, and weight pointed companies by relevance instead of rank alone. Optionally set a min_scores.final floor so weak queries add no pointers.

checked.statement: types filters fact types (world, experience, observation). prefer_observations drops raw facts that a returned observation was consolidated from, and backfills the freed slots. Atlas sends neither, so results mix observations, which need the two-hop resolution, with facts that duplicate them.
checked.quote: When recalling raw facts ('world'/'experience') together with 'observation', drop any raw fact that an observation in the results was consolidated from
checked.atlas_today: All types, no dedup.
checked.opportunity: For pointer recalls, either types=["world"] (each hit carries document_id and metadata inline, so it is a direct section pointer) or prefer_observations=true with include.source_facts, so slots are not spent on duplicates.

checked.statement: Each fact carries chunk_id. include.chunks returns the chunk text keyed by chunk_id, and GET /chunks/{chunk_id} returns chunk_text and chunk_index. Atlas parses chunk_id but nothing uses it. It points the Investigator at the section, then picks the window that best matches the memory text.
checked.quote: chunk_id: str | None = None
checked.atlas_today: chunk_id parsed, unused. No chunk reads.
checked.opportunity: Use the fact's chunk (at most retain_chunk_size, 3000 chars by default) to place a pointer inside a long section exactly, instead of a best-match window. The docs do not say whether chunk_text is a verbatim substring of the retained content, so check before relying on offsets.

checked.statement: GET /entities/graph returns entity nodes (with mention counts) and co-occurrence edges (with weight and lastCooccurred). It is bank-wide, with limit and min_count only and no tag filter. GET /entities lists entities by mention count. The entity observations returned with them are deprecated and empty.
checked.quote: Return a graph of entities (nodes) and their co-occurrences (edges) for visualization.
checked.atlas_today: Never called.
checked.opportunity: Use it as a candidate-pair index: universe company or counterparty entities that co-occur with a seed company's entity are companies to read next, and the duplicates it shows reveal entity fragmentation. It stays a reading pointer only, since co-mention forms no edge under Atlas's rules.

checked.statement: Atlas's reflect sends only query, tags scope, include.facts and an optional response_schema. budget is left at the schema default 'low' and max_tokens at 4096. Mental models are not excluded, so a reflect may lean on the Theme status/Bottlenecks models, whose content is not resolved like memories. fact_types, tag_groups and include.tool_calls are unused.
checked.quote: body: dict[str, Any] = {"query": query, **_scope_fields(scope)}
checked.atlas_today: Default budget (low). Mental models allowed. No trace.
checked.opportunity: Send budget explicitly (mid/high for research questions). Consider exclude_mental_models=true, or exclude_mental_model_ids, when citations must resolve to Source Versions. Use include.tool_calls when diagnosing thin answers.

checked.statement: GET /stats reports pending_consolidation, failed_consolidation (permanently failed, recoverable via POST /consolidation/recover), total_observations, last_consolidated_at, last_memory_write_at and links_by_link_type.
checked.quote: Number of source memories (world/experience) whose consolidation permanently failed and can be retried via the consolidation recovery endpoint.
checked.atlas_today: Never called. Atlas polls its own operations only.
checked.opportunity: Watch pending and failed consolidation (facts never consolidated never appear as observations), and recover failed ones. Compare a mental model's last_memory_seen_at (dropped today) with last_memory_write_at.

checked.statement: GET /tags lists unique tags with memory counts and supports '*' wildcards (e.g. company:*), from memories or mental models.
checked.quote: List all unique tags in a memory bank with usage counts. Supports wildcard search using '*'
checked.atlas_today: Never called.
checked.opportunity: A cheap memory-coverage check per company, form or source for the Theme explorer's coverage gaps and for deciding which companies' filings to retain next.

checked.statement: GET /memories/{id}/history returns the full history of an observation, with each change's source facts resolved to their text. The response is untyped in the OpenAPI and was never recorded.
checked.quote: Get the full history of an observation, with each change's source facts resolved to their text.
checked.atlas_today: Never called.
checked.opportunity: Show how the bank's view of a company changed and which new facts changed it. These are pointers for the Skeptic to read as candidate contradictions; the text is never quoted.

checked.statement: RetainRequest accepts a client-supplied operation_id. Re-submitting with the same ID returns the original operation and creates no new work.
checked.quote: Re-submitting with the same operation_id returns the original operation and creates no new work, so retrying after a lost or timed-out acknowledgement will not enqueue a duplicate.
checked.atlas_today: Not sent. A retried retain job after a lost acknowledgement re-submits, and the per-version document_id upsert pays extraction again.
checked.opportunity: Derive a deterministic UUID per (source version, batch) so retries never double-spend the retain budget.

checked.statement: MemoryItem.strategy picks a named retain strategy, defined in bank config retain_strategies, for one item. Mixed strategies in one async batch produce several operations, returned in operation_ids.
checked.quote: Operation IDs when items were submitted as multiple strategy groups (async=true with mixed per-item strategies).
checked.atlas_today: No strategy. RetainSubmitted keeps only operation_id.
checked.opportunity: Extraction could differ by section kind (e.g. verbose for customer/supplier concentration and MD&A). If adopted, the gateway must keep and poll every ID in operation_ids.

checked.statement: POST /memories/dry-run-extract runs fact extraction only, with no storage or resolution. It accepts overrides for retain_mission, extraction mode, chunk size, entity_labels and strategy, and returns facts with raw entity names plus the chunks.
checked.quote: Preview what the retain step would extract from text WITHOUT changing the bank
checked.atlas_today: Never called.
checked.opportunity: A/B the template's retain_mission or entity labels on real 10-K sections before changing the bank. It costs one extraction call per test and stores nothing.

checked.topic: reflect scope hides Atlas's mental models
checked.statement: With non-empty tags and any_strict/all_strict, reflect's search_mental_models sees only mental models whose tags match. Atlas scopes every reflect any_strict on company:/theme: tags and its two models are untagged, so no Atlas reflect ever consults Theme status or Bottlenecks. Untagged directives still apply.
checked.quote: | Non-empty `tags`, `any_strict` or `all_strict` | Matching tagged data only | Matching tagged models only | Matching tagged directives plus untagged/global directives |
checked.atlas_today: SCOPE_MATCH = "any_strict" in backend/atlas/research/service.py; decisions.md 2026-09-29: "Both have `max_tokens` 2048, no tags (the bank holds only Atlas-retained, tagged material)".
checked.opportunity: Decide deliberately. Either tag both models theme:photonics, so a theme-scoped reflect sees them while refresh still reads the same theme-tagged memories through all_strict. Or keep them hidden on purpose, because an answer built on a model cites based_on.mental_models, which Atlas cannot resolve to a Source Version section.

checked.statement: budget controls how deeply the reflect agent explores. `low` is the default and is a shallow search. Only `high` explores all knowledge levels and tries several query variations to find indirect connections. The docs give no iteration or token figures per level.
checked.quote: At `low`, the agent does a shallow search optimized for speed. At `mid`, it checks multiple sources when the question warrants it. At `high`, it performs deep exploration across all knowledge levels and may use multiple query variations to find indirect connections.
checked.atlas_today: backend/atlas/hindsight/gateway.py reflect sends no budget: `body: dict[str, Any] = {"query": query, **_scope_fields(scope)}`, so every Atlas reflect runs at `low`.
checked.opportunity: Add budget to ReflectRequest and the gateway. Default to mid, and use high for multi-hop supply-chain questions and the replay question set. Measure token use from the response's usage field.

checked.statement: Reflect is an agentic tool loop: search_mental_models first, then search_observations, then recall over raw facts as the fallback, plus expand for more context, then done. It runs at most 10 iterations, must gather evidence before it answers, and only IDs it actually retrieved can be cited. A stale model does not short-circuit the loop, and a stale observation is checked against the raw facts.
checked.quote: 2. **Uses hierarchical retrieval** — Checks mental models first, then observations, then raw facts
checked.atlas_today: Atlas uses reflect only for the reflect job and for mental-model refreshes. Its scope excludes the models (see the first finding), so in practice its reflects start at observations.
checked.opportunity: Expect reflect citations to be mostly observations, as the spike observed. That keeps the two-hop resolution through source_memory_ids central.

checked.statement: By default, search_observations returns only the consolidated observation text. With HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_SOURCE_FACTS_MAX_TOKENS set (or the per-bank reflect_source_facts_max_tokens field in the template schema), it also returns the world facts each observation rests on.
checked.quote: if `HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_SOURCE_FACTS_MAX_TOKENS` is enabled — off by default — observation search also returns each observation's grounding facts.
checked.atlas_today: Not set in configs/hindsight/bank-template.json.
checked.opportunity: Set reflect_source_facts_max_tokens in the template's bank section. Reflect and refreshes would then see the exact figures and periods behind each belief, which supports the 'Never fabricate figures' directive, and could cite world facts that resolve in one hop. The cost is more context tokens per reflect.

checked.statement: Unless exclude_mental_models is set, a mental model's refresh can synthesise from sibling models. Knowledge pages turn this off by default to prevent a feedback loop in which one wrong claim spreads across documents.
checked.quote: | `exclude_mental_models: true` | A page never reflects on sibling pages. Without this, pages would cite each other and drift into a feedback loop where one wrong claim propagates across the knowledge base. |
checked.atlas_today: Both template models leave exclude_mental_models unset (false). Atlas's parser drops the 'mental-models' group from based_on (`_NON_MEMORY_BASED_ON = frozenset({"directives", "mental-models"})` in backend/atlas/hindsight/models.py), so a citation of a sibling model disappears silently.
checked.opportunity: Add "exclude_mental_models": true to both triggers, and to any future per-company or per-layer model.

checked.statement: A mental-model refresh is a full reflect run: retrieval plus the agentic loop of up to 10 iterations, plus one structured-output pass if the trigger has a schema. A dry run costs the same. Reading a model is only a database read.
checked.quote: A refresh is a full reflect run: retrieval plus an agentic LLM loop.
checked.atlas_today: Two models are refreshed daily on Hindsight's 06:00 cron. Atlas's job at 06:30 usually skips with min_interval or not_stale. The Scout reads Bottlenecks as a free GET.
checked.opportunity: Price each additional model at one reflect per day on which its scope changed. In the spike, one reflect took about 24-28 s and about 10.6k input and 1.9k output tokens on a tiny bank.

checked.statement: Both automatic triggers check whether any memory in the model's resolved scope (tags, tags_match, tag_groups, fact_types) is newer than its last refresh, and skip with no LLM call if none is. Memories not yet consolidated count as new. Deletions do not.
checked.quote: Both automatic triggers run the same check before spending an LLM call: **is there a memory in this model's resolved scope newer than its last refresh?**
checked.atlas_today: Atlas reads is_stale and skips not_stale models. Its models are untagged, so their scope is the whole bank and any retain makes them stale.
checked.opportunity: Narrowly scoped models (per company) are free on days without new filings, which makes many small models cheap.

checked.statement: Atlas's codex budget counts units only from hindsight_operation rows (retain/reprocess batches) and replay operations. reflect and refresh_mental_model jobs are held when the window is spent but never add a unit, and Hindsight's own refresh_cron runs outside Atlas's queue.
checked.quote: "SELECT h.id AS source_id, 1 AS units FROM hindsight_operation h"
checked.atlas_today: refresh.py: "Hindsight's own `refresh_cron` (06:00 UTC in the template) is gated by the same minimum". decisions.md accepts that the cron is not pause-aware. With 2 models the gap is small.
checked.opportunity: Before adding models, record one codex unit per reflect and per submitted refresh. Also consider letting Atlas's job be the only scheduler: give Hindsight a far-off cron and refresh through Atlas, so refreshes are counted and pausable.

checked.topic: structured output on a mental model
checked.statement: trigger.response_schema makes every refresh store a structured_output next to the markdown, extracted from the final stored document. If the extraction fails, the refresh fails and the previous content is kept.
checked.quote: If a `response_schema` is configured but the structured extraction cannot be produced, the refresh **fails** rather than silently persisting content with no structured view.
checked.atlas_today: No response_schema on either model. The Scout gets Bottlenecks as quoted markdown (backend/atlas/discovery/service.py _gaps).
checked.opportunity: Give Bottlenecks a schema: constraints with layer, status confirmed/unconfirmed, missing_evidence[], and companies, using explicit *_known booleans because union types return 500. The Scout and the Theme explorer could then use structured gaps.

checked.topic: mental model tags and refresh scope
checked.statement: A tagged model's refresh reads with all_strict by default: a memory must carry every one of the model's tags, and untagged memories are excluded. trigger.tags_match or tag_groups override this. tag_groups are boolean expressions that replace flat tags entirely.
checked.quote: If the mental model has tags, that reflect call uses `all_strict` tag matching — meaning it will only read memories that carry **all** of the mental model's tags. Untagged memories are excluded.
checked.atlas_today: Every memory carries company:<uuid>, theme:<slug>, source:, doctype: and form: tags. There are no layer tags.
checked.opportunity: A per-company model tagged company:<uuid> reads exactly that company's memories. A per-layer model can use tag_groups (any) over the company: tags of the companies in that layer, without adding a layer tag at retain time. It then misses layer statements in other companies' filings.

checked.statement: delta mode edits a structured document with typed operations, copies untouched sections byte for byte, reads only memories created since the last refresh, and accumulates based_on across refreshes. It never writes a partial document. The docs suggest a periodic clear plus refresh to undo drift.
checked.quote: A delta refresh scopes its retrieval to memories created since the last refresh, so the LLM reads genuinely new information rather than re-reading the whole bank.
checked.atlas_today: Both models use the default, full mode, with fact_types unset (world, experience and observation).
checked.opportunity: Keep full mode for Bottlenecks, which has to re-judge every constraint each time. Consider delta with fact_types [observation] for long per-company models to cut cost, with a weekly clear plus refresh. Try it with dry-run-refresh first, which costs as much as a real refresh.

checked.statement: Directives affect only reflect, and so also mental-model refreshes. Untagged directives apply to every reflect. Tagged ones apply only when the request's tags match, unless apply_all_directives is true.
checked.quote: - **Untagged directives always apply**, on every `reflect`.
