checked.atlas_today: Five untagged directives (cite evidence, say what's missing, never fabricate figures, flag source uncertainty, no trading orders) apply to every reflect and refresh. This matches the docs' guardrail use.
checked.opportunity: Tagged directives could add theme-specific rules, for example a theme:photonics rule that applies the second-source-and-pricing-power test, and they would load automatically on theme-scoped reflects.

checked.statement: reflect_mission and the disposition traits affect only reflect, and the mission goes into the system prompt. The docs describe the mission as a first-person identity narrative. Their Research Assistant preset is skepticism 4, literalism 3, empathy 3.
checked.quote: A first-person narrative that provides identity and framing context for `reflect`. The agent uses this to ground its reasoning and apply a consistent perspective.
checked.atlas_today: configs/hindsight/bank-template.json has an imperative mission ("Form source-grounded research syntheses. ... Seek disconfirmation."), skepticism 4, literalism 4, and empathy unset (3).
checked.opportunity: Rewrite the mission as an identity ("You are a supply-chain research analyst ..."). Consider empathy 1-2. Check the result with POST /prompts/preview {"operation":"reflect"}, which makes no LLM call.

checked.statement: Reflect's based_on (with include.facts) has memories (world, experience, observation; no document_id), mental_models and directives. A mental model's stored reflect_response.based_on is grouped by fact type instead, as recorded in 0.10.1.
checked.quote: - `memories` — a list of memory facts (world, experience, observation) that were retrieved and cited. Each item has `id`, `text`, `type`, `context`, `occurred_start`, and `occurred_end`.
checked.atlas_today: Atlas flattens both shapes (models.py _flatten_based_on, _memories_in_based_on) and resolves memories in two hops.
checked.opportunity: none

checked.statement: Observed in 0.10.1: reflect can put content from raw chunks into its answer without citing any memory ID for it.
checked.quote: Reflect can answer from raw chunks as well as facts (bake-off: a table figure absent from facts appeared in reflect output).
checked.atlas_today: Atlas checks each double-quoted passage against the archived text, but an unquoted figure that came from a chunk stays unverified.
checked.opportunity: For mental models, include_chunks: false on the trigger (or fact_types [observation], which removes the recall tool) keeps the content to citable memories.

checked.statement: A knowledge page is a mental model with preset defaults (delta, observations only, exclude sibling models, refresh after consolidation, max_tokens 4096), plus a folder tree and page search (BM25 plus vector, fused by RRF, no reranking). Pages are not in the bank-template manifest. The bank field knowledge_page_default_trigger can make new pages cron-driven.
checked.quote: A knowledge page *is* a [mental model](./mental-models). Same synthesis, same background refresh, same provenance.
checked.atlas_today: Not used (decisions.md: 'No knowledge pages in Phase 2').
checked.opportunity: Little gain over mental models with the same trigger fields. Pages would need their own API calls and a cron default, because their refresh_after_consolidation default breaks Atlas's no-runaway rule.

checked.statement: For every discovery, the Scout reads the current Bottlenecks content, whatever the investigation's as_of is.
checked.quote: gaps, gaps_source = self._gaps()
checked.atlas_today: _gaps() ignores as_of, so a back-dated investigation's Scout sees gaps synthesised from later filings. Replay banks import no models and are unaffected.
checked.opportunity: Skip the gaps when as_of is in the past, or use the history entry dated before as_of. The history endpoint keeps up to 50 previous versions.

checked.statement: By default an observation is scoped to all of a memory's tags combined. Atlas's memories carry company, theme, source, doctype and form tags and send no observation_scopes, so observations never merge across companies or across forms. Cross-company synthesis happens only inside a theme model's reflect.
checked.quote: By default, observations are scoped to all of a memory's tags combined.
checked.atlas_today: backend/atlas/retention/service.py version_tags adds company:, theme:, source:, doctype: and form:. There is no observation_scopes anywhere in backend/.
checked.opportunity: The lead owns observations. Note that a theme or layer model with fact_types [observation] would read only per-company, per-form beliefs.

checked.statement: A refresh that fails appends a history entry with kind refresh_failed, a failure_reason and previous_content null.
checked.quote: Those runs now append a failure record carrying the reason and the exception.
checked.atlas_today: MentalModelRevision in backend/atlas/hindsight/models.py ignores kind, so a failure record shows up as a revision with empty content.
checked.opportunity: Parse kind and failure_reason, and show failure records separately.

checked.statement: Since 0.8.5, retain can be set to fail when any fact-extraction error occurs. By default (false), an operation in which some chunks failed extraction is still marked 'completed', so the facts those chunks would have produced vanish without notice. The setting is static and applies to the whole server.
checked.quote: | `HINDSIGHT_API_FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS` | When `true`, a retain operation that accumulated any fact-extraction errors is marked `failed`
checked.atlas_today: Atlas detects only sections with zero facts (reprocessed once, then marked `zero_fact`). A long Item section is many 3,000-char extraction chunks, and losing some of them is not detected.
checked.opportunity: Ask the owner to set HINDSIGHT_API_FAIL_ON_EXTRACTION_ERRORS=true on the shared server (it affects hermes too). Alternatively, Atlas could compare each section's memory count with its length to flag sections that yielded too few facts.

checked.statement: Entities are never linked to each other directly. They connect only by being attached to the same memory. Recall starts from semantic hits and expands through shared entities, precomputed semantic links between memories, and extracted causal links (causes/caused_by/enables/prevents). A supplier or customer direction exists only inside the fact text.
checked.quote: No. In Hindsight, entities (people, places, concepts, or classification labels) do not have direct arrows connecting them to one another.
checked.atlas_today: Atlas builds its own typed, directed Relationships from Assertions. Memory serves as the reading index (reading pointers).
checked.opportunity: Don't expect Hindsight's graph to stand in for supply-chain edges. Multi-hop recall works only to the extent that the same company resolves to the same entity across documents (see the entities finding).

checked.statement: Since 0.9.2, a retain item can carry `entities` (combined with the auto-extracted ones) and `resolve_entities`. When `resolve_entities` is false, the given names are taken literally. Separately, 0.9.2 stopped entity merges based only on history-matched names, and 0.9.0 improved deduplication within a batch.
checked.quote: Retain and update_memory can now optionally resolve entities via a dedicated flag, enabling more controlled entity handling.
checked.atlas_today: RetainItem sends content, document_id, timestamp, context, metadata and tags. It sends no entities.
checked.opportunity: Pass the filer's canonical name, and the universe companies a section names, as entities. Then 'Lumentum', 'Lumentum Holdings Inc.' and 'LITE' anchor to one entity node, which is the path graph expansion and multi-hop pointers follow.

checked.topic: model split: routing changes only extraction
checked.statement: Metadata routing (0.10.0) picks only the member that extracts an item. Recall, reflect, consolidation, mental-model refresh and dry-run extraction all stay on the primary LLM. Routing is applied per item, nothing about it is stored, and reprocess replays the original metadata. Separate CONSOLIDATION_LLM_* and per-operation chains exist, and MENTAL_MODEL_REFRESH inherits the reflect chain. The docs say nothing on whether mixing an extraction model with a different consolidation model is a problem.
checked.quote: It is not a data boundary: the facts extracted from a routed document are stored in the same bank as everything else, and recall, reflect, consolidation, mental-model refresh and dry-run extraction all continue to use the primary LLM.
checked.atlas_today: ATLAS_RETAIN_EXTRACTOR=minimax routes Atlas's retains to MiniMax. Consolidation, reflect and mental-model refresh run on the shared primary, openai-codex, which Atlas does not count against any budget.
checked.opportunity: Accept that consolidation quality and quota stay on Codex. If observation quality matters, the owner could set a CONSOLIDATION_* chain, but that is server-wide.

checked.topic: Codex primary: reflect breaks when the token is shared
checked.statement: When a long-running Hindsight shares ~/.codex/auth.json with another Codex process, a rotated single-use refresh token makes /reflect fail while recall and /health keep working. The fix is a dedicated CODEX_HOME; 0.10.0 added a separate credential directory for each Codex member.
checked.quote: Recall and `/health` keep working (the database and API are fine), but
checked.atlas_today: The shared server's primary is Codex, whose quota is shared with hermes, the Codex CLI and LiteLLM's ChatGPT alias (docs/decisions.md). Atlas's reflect, mental-model refresh and the consolidation behind its observations all depend on that primary.
checked.opportunity: Treat a reflect failure while recall succeeds as a credential problem rather than an outage, and confirm with the owner that the Hindsight pod has its own CODEX_HOME.

checked.statement: A model that isn't in the tested list must support at least 65,000 output tokens. RETAIN_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS defaults to 64000 and must exceed RETAIN_CHUNK_SIZE (3000). MiniMax-M3 is the `minimax` provider's default model, but it is not in the 'Tested Models' table, and its output ceiling is not documented.
checked.quote: Other LLM models not listed above may work with Hindsight, but they must support **at least 65,000 output tokens** to ensure reliable fact extraction.
checked.atlas_today: Atlas extracts with MiniMax-M3 with thinking disabled. The bake-off found 16 of 17 expected facts, using two small documents.
checked.opportunity: Check MiniMax-M3's real output limit through LiteLLM. If it is lower, the server's RETAIN_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS must be lowered, or long chunks could be truncated.

checked.statement: Indexed chain members take their own EXTRA_BODY. No fallback to the global value is listed (unlike _REASONING_EFFORT, which falls back). The bake-off found that MiniMax-M3's thinking is disabled only through EXTRA_BODY when it sits behind provider=openai.
checked.quote: | `HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_<n>_EXTRA_BODY` / `_DEFAULT_HEADERS` | Per-member JSON overrides. | - |
checked.atlas_today: unknown: the shared server's member-1 settings live in home-ops PR #7180, which is not in this repo.
checked.opportunity: Confirm with the owner that HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_1_EXTRA_BODY disables MiniMax thinking. Otherwise routed extraction runs with thinking on, which was never tested and is slower.

checked.topic: observation dedup and proof count are not independence
checked.statement: Since 0.8.0, consolidation merges near-duplicate observations semantically, and this is on by default. Each observation references its source memories and carries a proof count. So a statement repeated across many filings by the same company becomes one observation with a high proof count.
checked.quote: **Evidence tracking**: Each observation references the source memories (with exact quotes) that support it, plus a proof count
checked.atlas_today: Atlas resolves observations through source_memory_ids and judges independence by Evidence Family, not by Hindsight.
checked.opportunity: Never read an observation's proof count or number of sources as corroboration. Repeated 10-K/10-Q boilerplate inflates it.

checked.topic: reflect answers from mental models first
checked.statement: Reflect checks mental models before observations and raw facts. Since 0.8.0 it skips its extra LLM call when a fresh mental model can answer directly. ReflectRequest supports exclude_mental_models and exclude_mental_model_ids.
checked.quote: Reflect checks mental models first, so a fresh one can answer without descending into observations and raw facts.
checked.atlas_today: The reflect body is query, tags, tags_match, include.facts and an optional response_schema. It never excludes the Theme status or Bottlenecks models.
checked.opportunity: Pass exclude_mental_models for research reflects whose citations must resolve to Source Version sections. Whether a tag-scoped reflect uses the untagged models is not documented.

checked.statement: 0.8.4 added prefer_observations (drops raw facts an observation in the results supersedes and backfills the freed slots), per-stage scores, min_scores and recency decay. 0.9.2 added an explicit temporal_window. Recency is anchored on query_timestamp. max_tokens defaults to 4096.
checked.quote: Recall supports configurable recency decay (linear, exponential, or none) to tune ranking toward recent memory.
checked.atlas_today: The recall body is query, budget (default 'mid'), tags and tags_match. It sends no query_timestamp, prefer_observations, max_tokens or scores, and pointer weight is 1/rank.
checked.opportunity: Send query_timestamp equal to the investigation's as_of, so recency is scored from the research date. Try prefer_observations, so each pointer recall reaches more distinct sections. Consider a higher max_tokens or budget for pointer recalls.

checked.statement: Since 0.10.0, reflect no longer gives a value for a period the memories don't cover. It says the data isn't recorded instead of extrapolating from neighbouring periods. Also since 0.10.0, reflect fails when its retrieval tools fail, and since 0.9.2 it fails when it produces no answer.
checked.quote: Reflect no longer states a specific value for a period the memories don't cover — it says the data isn't recorded instead of extrapolating a number from neighbouring periods.
checked.atlas_today: The bank template's 'Never fabricate figures' directive asks for the same thing.
checked.opportunity: none; expect more 'not recorded' answers, and more failed reflect jobs where earlier versions returned partial answers.

checked.topic: metadata goes into the extraction prompt
checked.statement: Item metadata is not a filter. It is included in the fact-extraction prompt as context and returned with every recalled memory.
checked.quote: **Included in the fact extraction prompt**, so the LLM can use it as additional context when extracting facts
checked.atlas_today: The metadata is source_version_id, section_anchor, char_start, char_end, available_at, and extractor when set. These are IDs and offsets the extractor can't use; form, company and period reach it only through context ('<title>: <heading>').
checked.opportunity: Add human-readable keys (company display name, form, fiscal period, filer role) that help the extractor attribute and date facts, while keeping the provenance keys.

checked.topic: entity labels as hard recall filters
checked.statement: An entity-label group with tag: true writes each extracted label as a tag, which then works as a SQL-level filter before ranking. 0.10.0 added multi-valued open-text labels.
checked.quote: This is a SQL-level filter applied before ranking, not a scoring signal — the excluded memories never enter the retrieval pipeline.
checked.atlas_today: Tags are set only by Atlas (company, theme, source, document type, form). The bank template defines no entity labels.
checked.opportunity: Have the extractor label each fact with a supply-chain layer or statement kind (capacity, customer, supply agreement) so pointer recall can be filtered hard by layer. This needs a template change and only applies to facts retained afterwards.

checked.statement: Since 0.8.6, an async retain accepts a client-supplied operation_id. Resubmitting with the same ID returns the original operation and creates no new work.
checked.quote: Retain: async retries are now idempotent via caller-supplied operation_id.
checked.atlas_today: The retain_batch body is only items + async (`"items": [item.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True) for item in items],`), so a lost acknowledgement leads to a second operation.
checked.opportunity: Send a deterministic UUID per (job, attempt-batch) as operation_id, so a timed-out submit doesn't cause a duplicate extraction that spends budget.

checked.statement: Async retain splits large batches into sub-batches and extracts in RETAIN_CHUNK_SIZE pieces (3,000 characters by default), each producing about 17 facts. Larger chunks mean fewer LLM calls but may lose context. The docs disagree on whether the 10,000 split threshold counts tokens or characters.
checked.quote: | `HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_CHUNK_SIZE` | Max characters per chunk for fact extraction. Larger chunks extract fewer LLM calls but may lose context. | `3000` |
checked.atlas_today: Atlas sends whole SEC Item sections as single items. Other text goes in chunks of at most 12,000 chars. Hindsight then re-chunks every item at 3,000 chars.
checked.opportunity: none on Atlas's side. Content-loss bugs with oversized items were fixed in 0.8.3 and 0.10.0, and a section's extraction quality depends on 3,000-char windows, not on Atlas's sectioning.

checked.statement: Vector search takes 10-50 ms on 100K+ facts, and the docs say it has been tested with millions of facts per bank. A recall takes 50-100 ms without a reranker and 200-500 ms with one. The reranker considers up to 300 candidates by default.
checked.quote: - **Typical query time**: 10-50ms for vector search on 100K+ facts
checked.atlas_today: Atlas reranks remotely through LiteLLM's `rerank` model and runs one recall per Scout query.
checked.opportunity: none; at Atlas's scale (filings for 12 companies), bank size won't make recall slow.

checked.statement: 0.10.0 fixed retain chunk-ID collisions between banks, and 0.9.1 fixed document statements being shared across banks.
checked.quote: Retain operations no longer risk chunk ID collisions between banks.
checked.atlas_today: Atlas retains the same srcv: document IDs into the research bank and into throwaway evaluation banks on the same server.
checked.opportunity: none on 0.10.x; this is why evaluation banks on the shared server are safe now.

checked.statement: A pending_consolidation counter that never falls usually means operations claimed by a worker that no longer exists, because HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_ID is unstable. The Helm StatefulSet sets a stable ID.
checked.quote: The root cause is almost always an unstable `HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_ID`.
checked.atlas_today: The local compose sets HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_ID: atlas-hindsight-1. The cluster uses Helm.
checked.opportunity: When observations stop appearing, check /banks/{id}/stats pending_consolidation before blaming the LLM.

checked.statement: The default embedder and reranker are English-only, and native BM25 uses PostgreSQL's English dictionary, which gives poor non-English results and no CJK tokenization.
checked.quote: The default `native` backend uses PostgreSQL's English dictionary
checked.atlas_today: Atlas retains only English. Embeddings are qwen3-embedding-0.6b and reranking is LiteLLM `rerank`.
checked.opportunity: Only relevant if AMF (French) or HKEX (Chinese) documents are ever retained. That would need pgroonga and a multilingual reranker.

checked.statement: By default each retained memory's observations are consolidated in one scope made of all its tags, and existing observations are matched all_strict, so only observations whose tag set equals the scope are updated. Atlas sends no observation_scopes, so this default applies to every item.
checked.quote: During consolidation, Hindsight uses `all_strict` matching to find existing observations to update — only observations whose tags exactly match the current scope are considered.
checked.atlas_today: RetainItem has no observation_scopes field (extra="forbid"), so the default `combined` scope applies.
checked.opportunity: Send observation_scopes, e.g. [["theme:photonics"],["company:<uuid>"]] or "shared", so observations consolidate across forms and across companies. Check GET .../observations/scopes on production first.

checked.statement: Every retain item carries company, all themes of the company, source:<provider>, doctype:<source_type> and form:<form_type>. Under the combined default this probably splits observations by company × form × source: a company's 10-K facts apart from its 10-Q, 8-K and transcript facts, and nothing across companies. This is inferred from the docs, not observed.
checked.quote: tags.append(f"form:{version.form_type}")
checked.atlas_today: Tags are used only to scope recall and reflect (company/theme any_strict). source, doctype and form are never queried by Atlas's research reads.
checked.opportunity: Keep the provenance tags for filtering, but set observation_scopes so they are not a consolidation boundary.

checked.statement: All submitted sections of a Source Version go in one operation. When it ends non-completed with a non-transient error class, every pending section of that operation is set failed. No document is checked on this path, so sections a successful sub-batch extracted are still marked failed.
checked.quote: "retain_state = 'failed', error = :error",
checked.atlas_today: The poll job marks every pending row of the operation failed with the operation's error. child_operations are used only to classify the error.
checked.opportunity: Decide each section's outcome per document (GET /documents/{id}) even on a failed operation, or submit smaller batches, so one bad chunk does not fail a whole 10-K.

checked.statement: Only quota and outage texts are transient. Anything else, including a failure with no message, an LLM timeout ("timeout" / "timed out" is not matched) or a relayed 500, is permanent and final.
checked.quote: r"\b50[234]\b|service[ _-]?unavailable|bad gateway|gateway[ _-]?time-?out"
checked.atlas_today: Permanent failures are final: failed sections are not retried automatically. An owner-run retry_failed resets them to pending.
checked.opportunity: Classify extraction timeouts and context-length errors explicitly, and record the error text distribution before tuning.

checked.statement: An SEC primary document's Item is one Hindsight document of unbounded length, and Hindsight chunks it internally. Other text is cut into chunks of at most 12,000 characters.
checked.quote: Items aren't split further: a 140k-character Risk Factors section is one Hindsight document, and Hindsight chunks it internally.
checked.atlas_today: Large Items such as Risk Factors and MD&A go to Hindsight as single items in one batch per version.
checked.opportunity: Bound Item sections (sub-sections) to reduce per-item extraction failures and give finer pointer and provenance granularity.

checked.statement: After a completed operation, a section's fact count is GET /documents/{id}.memory_unit_count. 0 triggers one reprocess (re-retain under the same ID), then zero_fact. A 404 is failed. result_metadata such as extraction_errors_count is stored but never read.
checked.quote: counts[row["id"]] = self._gateway.get_document(document).memory_unit_count
checked.atlas_today: Zero facts lead to one reprocess, then the zero_fact state. Memory IDs are listed via memories/list?document_id and stored on the row.
checked.opportunity: Use extraction_errors_count to tell 'nothing material' from 'extraction failed'.

checked.statement: content is the exact slice of the recorded parsed text, timestamp is the version's available_at (filing/dissemination time, not the reporting period), context is '<title>: <heading or anchor>', and metadata holds source_version_id, section_anchor, char_start, char_end and available_at as strings (plus extractor when routed).
checked.quote: context=f"{version.title}: {heading or anchor}",
checked.atlas_today: For SEC the title is '<company> <form> filed <date>[, <exhibit type>]'. A chunk's context ends 'chunk-003', the cover's 'cover'. No fiscal period is in the context.
checked.opportunity: Add the fiscal period/report date to the context and consider passing entities (company display names) so extraction and entity resolution anchor on the universe.

checked.topic: fields Atlas never sends on retain
checked.statement: RetainItem allows only content, document_id, timestamp, context, metadata and tags. Entities, resolve_entities, observation_scopes, strategy and update_mode cannot be sent. The request has async: true and no client operation_id.
checked.quote: """One document of a retain batch (for Atlas: one section of a Source Version)."""
checked.atlas_today: Only the six modelled fields are sent. A crash between submit and record leads to a resubmission without an idempotency key.
checked.opportunity: Add entities (universe company names), observation_scopes and a client operation_id (idempotent retries).

checked.statement: Recall sends only query, budget (default mid) and tags plus tags_match (any_strict). It sends no types, max_tokens (server default 4096), include (chunks or source_facts), prefer_observations, query_timestamp, temporal_window or min_scores.
checked.quote: body: dict[str, JsonValue] = {"query": query, "budget": budget, **_scope_fields(scope)}
checked.atlas_today: API recall, Scout and Skeptic pointers, and replays all use this. Investigations scope by theme tag only.
checked.opportunity: Pass types/prefer_observations to control fact vs observation mix, include.source_facts to skip per-observation GETs, query_timestamp = as_of for recency anchoring, and max_tokens to control result count.

checked.statement: RecallResult keeps only 'results'. trace, entities, chunks and source_facts are dropped. Per memory, scores, entities and attachments are not modelled, and source_fact_ids (the recall's name for an observation's sources) is not read, so each recalled observation costs a GET /memories/{id}.
checked.quote: # A recall result carries no source IDs; the memory lookup does.
checked.atlas_today: Relevance scores and entities are discarded. Rank is the only relevance signal kept (in reading pointers).
